values: Mostly remains in 8 PIT and 9 FOUNTAIN.
Its sight and hearing are slightly worse than an average human’s.
It is not smart but is clever, learns from mistakes, and adopts better tactics with exposure.
If it finishes eating or loses track of the party, it heads to 9 FOUNTAIN for a bath.
When someone enters the center of 44 CISTERN, it starts swimming toward them.
One round after beginning its approach, it urinates in anticipation and fills the air with an ammonia stink.
On the following round, it loses patience and begins swimming on the surface.
When noisy wall-breaking vibrations reach it, it arrives in 5+1d4 minutes and waits on the cistern bottom near the mouth of the underwater tunnel.
It rests in 8 PIT 2-in-6 of the time.
Lvl 6; Def chain; Bite/Crush 1d8/1d18; Move slow; Climb slug; Str 9; Int 3; Dis hungry.
Immune to acid.
Torches and lanterns make it hesitate, but only a large fire scares it away.
If people try to run past it in a hallway or room, it makes both attacks.
Can climb out of 8 PIT in 2 rounds.
Carries 52 Nascent Lambfruit and 6 Immature Lambfruit.
Produces the exotic types of waste stored in the four pools of area 20.
Swims 10 feet per round.
Climbs the slick walls at 46 DAYLIGHT as fast as a human can.

The dungeon’s central predator, guarding and roaming between its pit and fountain.
The figure the characters must elude during the first half of the adventure.

place.module-lair-of-the-lamb.the-free-city-of-lon-barago
One of the three great temples that hold power in Lon Barago; it worships Vandoh, Goddess of Wisdom, Patience, Self-Improvement, and the powers behind the sun.
The organization above the cistern that receives water from the noria and may retaliate if its godling is expelled into its drinking fountain.

Anyone can become an Acrobat. Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and increases Nah to 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf. Dodge gives +2 Defense per empty inventory slot, capped at 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower, and does not stack with armor. Nah can declare once per day, or twice per day at Template C, that something physically dodgeable does not affect the Acrobat. Tricky makes a natural 20 attack deal double damage and grant a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver. Cat Power treats falls as 20 feet shorter and causes cats to tend to like the Acrobat. Roast the Oaf lets the Acrobat force a larger enemy that misses with a melee attack to make another melee attack against a target in range, potentially itself. Two copies of Tricky from two Acrobat and two Fighter levels combine into Very Tricky.
One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
Anyone can become a Barbarian without first unlocking the class through play.
Each level of Barbarian grants +2 Loincloth HP. Advancement grants Rage at A, Firewater at B, Thews 1/day at C, and Rampage plus Thews 2/day at D.
One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
Anyone can become a Fighter without first unlocking the class through play.
Each level of Fighter grants +1 Attack. Advancement grants Stand Tough at A, Tricky at B, Very Tricky at C, and Double Attack at D.
One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.

In this introductory adventure, every player controls multiple level 0 peasants. They have no special abilities and die in a single hit; the multiple peasants give players "extra lives" while they learn the system.

The game begins with 12 level 0 peasants in a dungeon. Unless there are more than 6 players, each player controls multiple peasants. Each player chooses one controlled peasant as their PC; the remaining controlled peasants are hirelings.
Anyone can become a Thief without first unlocking the class through play.
Each level of Thief grants +1 Mastery and +1 Stealth. Advancement grants “Luck” at A, Opportunist at B, Preparation at C, and Snag at D.
One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
Reaching freedom outside the dungeon counts as a Milestone.
Removing the heavy bar from 21 HEAVY DOORS grants a Milestone because the party has escaped from the Lamb, unless the Lamb has already been killed.
Escaped from the Lamb Milestone
Escaping the Dungeon Is a Milestone
Anyone with a lobster claw is Favored by Vandoh.
If all ghouls are killed, the character whose left hand was possessed becomes Favored by Vandoh; the source points to Appendix D for the full effect.
If all seven mummies are reassembled and returned, or close enough, the character who took the most initiative becomes Favored by Vandoh; Appendix C contains the referenced rules.
A Treasure called the Abacus of Vandoh is inside the opened Stone Egg; the source points to Appendix A for its full description.
A Treasure located in 39 STONE EGG and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.

A maple, shale, and lapis-lazuli abacus that can perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and certain types of square roots. Three times per day it answers a question whose answer is an integer from 2 through 9. The GM secretly rolls d100: 11–100 gives the honest answer, 2–9 gives that rolled number, and 1 or 10 gives no response. It cannot answer about things more than 100 feet away; it only understands obdurate physical things, cannot read minds or understand names, struggles to distinguish humans, and cannot understand questions longer than 12 words.

A spellbook whose covers and pages are polished iron sheets, with letters formed by unpolished sections. A chain woven through its spine is intended to secure it to the owner’s waist. It is written in Cheoxic, permits a character to begin learning Cheoxic, contains the spells speak with dead and fear, and permits advancement as a Necromancer. Once the reader reaches Necromancer Level 1, the lich Shadrakul asks that character to become her apprentice.
The robed skeleton in 14A SHADRAKUL offers a black iron spellbook; once it is held, the sarcophagus trapdoor locks open. See Appendix A.
A roll of 18 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a bottle of liquid hole; see Appendix A.

A vial of utterly black oil that bends light toward itself, produces a lensing effect in the surrounding air, and has no smell. Tasting it creates a large piercing-like hole in the tongue. Applied to a surface, it creates a hole up to 6 inches wide and 5 feet deep, never wider than half the object; created holes cannot intersect. Applied to a portcullis, it can make the bars resemble Swiss cheese without breaking them. Consuming it creates a hole in the abdomen and causes the consumer’s guts to fall out.
Bottle of Liquid Hole
Liquid Hole
A Treasure located in 42 SUNKEN GALLERY and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.

A hand mirror shaped like the outline of a woman’s face, including ears and carefully styled hair. Its holder chooses what appears in the mirror; it can display anything the holder imagines, including an honest reflection.
The crone's coffer contains the hand mirror of lies, a Treasure whose full description is in Appendix A.
A harpoon leans against the east wall in 33 FUNGUS.
Harpoons are one of the suggested tools that can be combined with other tactics to kill the Lamb in the cistern.
Burning oil is a suggested weapon against the Lamb in the cistern. The rowboat at 45 BARRELS contains 2 flasks of oil.
Key light sources include 1 oil in room 5 and 2 oil each in rooms 24, 30, and 45.

A silver orb about 1 inch across. It immediately forgives the bearer’s next significant sin, after which the orb corrodes. Orbs are sold but tightly controlled; the source states that finding one makes resale to the Church the only ethical option. It is worth 500s. Rumors claim that golden orbs can forgive even mortal sins.
The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries an Orb of Indulgence worth 500s.
A purple pouch in 4 CHESTS contains 2 doses of purple lotus powder; see Appendix D.
A small bag in 34 CACHE contains 2 doses of purple lotus powder; Appendix D is referenced.

A smoked drug that causes 1d3 hours of sleep. On waking, the GM rapidly presents, in random order, a fun dream, a dream of something that happened, a scary dream, and a dream of something likely to happen; at least one should be semi-useful. A smoker thereafter cannot sleep without more purple lotus powder unless they have remained sleepless for 3 nights.
Rooms 18A, 31, and 40 each contain 30' rope.
Ropes are one of the suggested tools that can be combined with other tactics to kill the Lamb in the cistern.
A Treasure located in 8 PIT and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.
Akina carries the Ruby Ring of Wisdom, worth 1000s, and offers it in exchange for rescue.
The lead-and-iron chest in 4 CHESTS contains only the Skull of Davok, which escapes when the chest is opened; see Appendix A.

The remnant of the demon Davok, resembling a deformed elephant skull. Once released from its lead-lined chest, it tries once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet (Cha Save or die). After absorbing flesh it regrows much of its head and voice, demands to be carried out, and casts geas until obeyed. It can spend an hour calling a carpet of vermin to carry it at a crawl; if it wanders this way, add Davok to the Random Encounter Table in place of Atmospheric Encounters for rooms 1–20. It awakens when touched or when its name is called. In combat it casts ignite for 3d6 fire damage (Dex for half) and polymorph with 3 MD. Taking 10 damage in one round stuns it for 1 minute while it reconstructs itself; nothing in this dungeon can destroy it. Returning it to the lead-lined chest makes it inert. Once free it searches for its missing body parts, and its loyal thrall becomes a warlock in Davok’s service, forcibly if necessary. The rest of the party may join Davok or leave; if they leave, the new warlock becomes an allied NPC in Lon Barago.
A small bag in 34 CACHE contains 3 doses of toad shavings; Appendix D is referenced.

A smoked drug. For 30 minutes, the user is so intoxicated that they cannot move independently or take actions, can speak with amphibians and reptiles, and experiences colors, patterns, and croaking noises as indescribably delightful.

Range 30 feet; target 1 creature; duration [sum] rounds. Each round the target declares three potential actions that are fully distinct, sharing no objects or verbs. Roll 1d3; the target performs the corresponding action. A save negates the spell. Splittable.
Vandress knows confusion.
Confusion
confusion
Father Bastoval has the spell delay; no spell mechanics are printed on this page.

Range 30 feet; target 1 effect; duration [dice] rounds. Delays an effect—something happening to one object because of an interaction with another object or spell. It can delay incoming damage or prevent a sword from breaking until later. It may be cast as a reaction outside the caster’s turn and takes no time. The spell can create paradoxes, which the GM is encouraged to resolve in the way most painful to the caster.
Delay
delay
One of the three Priests of the Pool knows emergency exit; each priest knows a different spell from sleep, desiccate, and emergency exit.

Range 30 feet; target object; duration 0. Teleports the target to a random room in the dungeon, random street in the city, or random adjacent hex. A Cha Save negates the spell. Dungeon rooms are selected by room number.
Emergency Exit
emergency exit
Father Bastoval has the spell haste; no spell mechanics are printed on this page.

Range 30 feet; target objects; duration 3 rounds. The target object or creature exists at double speed and ages 1d6 years. Human hair becomes permanently white. Creatures can make one extra attack each round. A save negates the spell. Splittable.
Haste
haste
Father Bastoval has the spell scry; no spell mechanics are printed on this page.

Range 10 feet; target point in space; duration 1 round. The caster astrally projects to a point designated by direction and distance. Each MD after the first may either make the astral form invisible or multiply the range by 10.
Scry
scry
One of the three Priests of the Pool knows sleep; each priest knows a different spell from sleep, desiccate, and emergency exit.
Range 30 feet; target creature; duration 0. The target must save or fall into a deep sleep. Noise does not wake the target, but a slap or kick does. Splittable.
Sleep
sleep

fields.text: In this introductory adventure, every player controls multiple level 0 peasants. They have no special abilities and die in a single hit; the multiple peasants give players "extra lives" while they learn the system.
fields.title: Level 0 Peasants

fields.text: If players find a way to skip or trivialize a combat, allow it. Combats are obstacles that may be manipulated as well as brute-forced, not mandatory encounters that must be consumed routinely.
fields.title: Allow Combat to Be Skipped or Trivialized

fields.text: Players will not find every secret area; resist the temptation to drop hints.
fields.title: Do Not Hint at Missed Secret Areas

fields.text: Do not impose the DM's morality on the players. Their actions have consequences, but conscientious or humanistic behavior must remain a player-driven choice, even if they choose to be murderhobos.
fields.title: Do Not Impose Morality

fields.text: Engagement increases when players receive meaningful decisions. Frame situations so the players have multiple viable options.
fields.title: Frame Multiple Viable Options

fields.text: When in doubt, give the players more information rather than less.
fields.title: Give More Information When in Doubt

fields.text: Track time. Actions such as digging through bone piles may cost only time; searching for useful items therefore spends torchlight and accepts the risk of random encounters.
fields.title: Keep Time Measures

fields.text: If a player makes a mistake or gets unlucky, allow the character to die rather than rescuing them and cheapening their choices. Conversely, allow lucky outcomes and good schemes that appear to "cheat" the game.
fields.title: Let Choices and Luck Matter

fields.text: Never fudge the dice or alter a creature or trap during an encounter. If combat is too difficult, the PCs can flee using Pursuit; if it is too easy, wrap it up quickly and move on using Morale.
fields.title: Never Fudge or Retune Mid-Encounter

fields.text: After the session, never tell players about what they missed. The dungeon's secrets must be earned through play or remain undiscovered.
fields.title: Do Not Reveal Missed Content after the Session

fields.text: Good play is not defined by strong character builds or thorough rules knowledge. It comes from being attentive, investigative, meticulous, scheming, and cowardly, except when a situation demands suicidal boldness.
fields.title: Reward Attentive and Investigative Play

fields.text: Horrible threats must leave players either an option to choose another path or options to recover. Presenting a sagging floor and asking whether they enter is an option; an unannounced lethal hazard resolved only by a Dexterity check is mere chance and offers no meaningful choice.
fields.title: Telegraph Danger and Provide Options

fields.text: Do not treat the dungeon as isolated rooms that each contain an encounter that must be resolved before continuing. The obstacle is the entire dungeon simultaneously, not only the current room.
fields.title: Treat the Whole Dungeon as the Obstacle

fields.text: The rulebook is never a higher authority than the DM. The "True GLOG" is the version the group builds for itself.
fields.title: DM Authority over the Rulebook

fields.text: Treat the GLOG as a philosophy rather than a single unified ruleset: take the rules you like, discard the rules you do not, and assemble the game suited to your group from many sources.
fields.title: The GLOG Is Modular

fields.text: Level 0 peasants are not initially provided with light sources or necessary tools, allowing mechanics, including the darkness rules, to be introduced one at a time.
fields.title: No Initial Light Sources or Necessary Tools

fields.text: Time is the enemy: torches burn down, the party has no food or water, and every 30 minutes carries a risk of a Random Encounter. Survival also requires taking time to investigate suspicious phenomena, so players must balance these competing needs.
fields.title: Balance Time Pressure against Investigation

fields.text: Information is used to find secrets, solve puzzles, and sidestep combats. Players acquire more information by asking questions about the environment and should try to ask a question in every room.
fields.title: Information Is a Resource

fields.text: The adventure contains over a dozen secret doors and hidden treasures, ranging from obvious to cryptic. None are essential, but all improve the party's odds of survival.
fields.title: Optional Secrets Improve Survival

fields.text: Many puzzles are solved by recognizing patterns or using mundane objects cleverly. Many have three or more solutions, and many problems can be solved with enough rope.
fields.title: Solve Puzzles with Patterns and Mundane Objects

fields.text: Players should spend more time choosing and planning battles than fighting them. Running away is often the right choice, and the most reliable ways to kill a monster do not rely on attack rolls.
fields.title: Plan, Avoid, or Flee Battles

fields.text: There are no social stats or abilities. To be effective, players must learn what creatures want, usually by asking them.
fields.title: Social Play without Social Stats

fields.text: The dungeon's rooms are tightly interlinked through backtracking, loops, and mapping. A solution to a puzzle or combat may be found in a later room, and an encounter need not be handled in the room where it occurs.
fields.title: Use the Dungeon's Interconnections

fields.text: The game begins with 12 level 0 peasants in a dungeon. Unless there are more than 6 players, each player controls multiple peasants. Each player chooses one controlled peasant as their PC; the remaining controlled peasants are hirelings.
fields.title: Level 0 Peasants

fields.text: Each peasant is defined by a profession. Roll a d20 for half of the peasants and a d100 for the other half. A peasant's profession counts as a Skill in which the character has 2 points.
fields.title: Profession

fields.text: Nearly all checks are against DC 16: roll a d20, add the relevant stat, and meet or exceed the DC. Saves are an exception and use Dex, Con, or Cha against DC 20. Cha is used for all magical effects and is the most common Save.
fields.title: Checks and Saves

fields.text: Generate Str, Dex, Con, Int, Wis, and Cha randomly in order. For each score, roll 3d6, divide the result by two, and round down. The average score is 5. The source states that there are four other stats.
fields.title: Level 0 Ability Score Generation

fields.text: To introduce non-binary genders, the source suggests replacing demographic results 7 and 13.
fields.title: Optional Non-Binary Demographic Results

fields.text: A child has Small Stature. Switch Str with the character's lowest ability score. Cramped spaces impose no penalty. The character does not have a Profession.
fields.title: Small Stature

fields.text: One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
fields.title: Acrobat

fields.text: One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
fields.title: Barbarian

fields.text: One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
fields.title: Fighter

fields.text: One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.
fields.title: Thief

fields.text: After 1 day without water, a character is dehydrated and takes -4 to all d20 rolls. After 3 days without water, the character dies.
fields.title: Dehydrated

fields.text: When a non-level-0 character takes damage beyond the amount remaining in HP, the excess becomes Lethal Damage; gaining any Lethal Damage makes the character fall unconscious and begin Dying. At 10 Lethal Damage, the character dies.
fields.title: Dying

fields.text: A Stabilized character wakes and can act normally, but remains at 0 HP and keeps all existing Lethal Damage.
fields.title: Stabilized

fields.text: Each day without food reduces maximum HP by 1, down to 0. Death from lack of food takes weeks.
fields.title: Starvation

fields.text: For a bow, mark one depletion after every encounter in which it is used. After three depletions, the ammunition is exhausted.
fields.title: Ammunition

fields.text: Provides +7 inventory slots.
fields.title: Backpack

fields.text: Provides +4 inventory slots.
fields.title: Burlap Sack

fields.text: Provides +10 inventory slots.
fields.title: Elfpack

fields.text: Attacks at -2 and deals 1d6 damage.
fields.title: Improvised Weapon

fields.text: Increase the weapon damage die by one step. Magical arms and armor can be broken only by magical foes.
fields.title: Magic Weapon

fields.text: It must be broken twice before its damage die is reduced by one step.
fields.title: Masterwork Weapon

fields.text: One ration is enough to feed the whole group.
fields.title: Ration

fields.text: Deals 1d6 damage.
fields.title: Regular Weapon

fields.text: When wielded by a character with Str 7 or more, increase the weapon damage die by one step.
fields.title: Two-Handed Weapon

fields.text: Each piece of armor gives +1 Defense. A piece of masterwork armor gives +2 Defense. A character cannot wear more than 3 pieces of armor.
fields.title: Armor

fields.text: The attack DC depends on the target's armor. Level 0 peasants have Atk 0. If multiple PCs attack the same target simultaneously and roll simultaneously, each gains +1 to the attack roll for every attacker beyond the first. The DC to defend against an enemy equals 12 + the attacker's Level. A character's Def score is determined entirely by armor.
fields.title: Attacking and Defending

fields.text: Combat maneuvers include actions such as tripping and shoving. First the enemy makes a free attack against the acting character; skip this step when the maneuver is the free maneuver granted by a critical hit. Then make an opposed Str or Dex check against DC 11 + the enemy's chosen Str or Dex, using whichever stats fit the maneuver. Success performs the maneuver.
fields.title: Combat Maneuvers

fields.text: A PC critical hit deals double damage or regular damage plus a free combat maneuver. A PC critical dodge takes no damage and allows a free combat maneuver or attack. An enemy critical hit deals double damage and makes a random piece of the target's armor lose 1 Def. An enemy critical dodge grants the enemy a free attack and breaks the attacker's weapon, reducing its damage die by one step. A masterwork weapon must be broken twice before its die shrinks. Only magical foes can break magical arms and armor.
fields.title: Critical Hits and Dodges

fields.text: Disposition describes what a creature wants and how it tends to act. The listed categories are examples rather than an exhaustive vocabulary; a custom disposition such as chivalrous should be interpreted according to its ordinary meaning.
fields.title: Disposition

fields.text: At dungeon speed, characters are assumed to listen at doors before opening them; the DM reports audible activity behind a door. A wooden door can be kicked in with a successful Str check in negligible time, but doing so makes Noise; failure takes 10 minutes. Metal doors cannot be kicked in. Locked doors require the appropriate key or lockpicks plus a successful Locksmith roll. Portcullises have fist-sized gaps and are normally locked down so Strength cannot raise them; a nearby ratchet winch often raises them in 1 minute, and they drop in 1 second. A portcullis may instead be locked open. A barred door opens only from the barred side; each bar is a piece of lumber weighing more than 100 pounds, and moving one alone requires a Str check.
fields.title: Doors

fields.text: A level 0 character dies upon taking any damage. Other characters convert damage beyond HP into Lethal Damage, fall unconscious, and start Dying. At the end of each round, a Dying character makes a Con check at DC 15 + current Lethal Damage. Reaching 10 Lethal Damage causes death. An ally can spend an action to Stabilize the character with an Int check against the same DC. Any amount of magical healing also Stabilizes. Stabilization wakes the character and allows normal actions, but HP remains 0 and Lethal Damage is unchanged. Resting in town while safe and fed removes 1 Lethal Damage.
fields.title: Dying

fields.text: The DM tracks time because it controls light depletion and random encounters. An exploration turn is 10 minutes. Dungeoneering actions usually take 1 exploration turn, including searching a room or body, prying a torch sconce from a wall, and passing through a room for the first time. This pace assumes cautious dungeon movement: whispering, examining details, testing each step, and listening.
fields.title: Exploration Time

fields.text: After 1 day without water, a character becomes dehydrated and takes -4 to all d20 rolls; after 3 days without water, the character dies. Each day without food reduces maximum HP by 1, down to 0; death takes weeks.
fields.title: Food and Water

fields.text: After a 10-minute rest, everyone recovers HP up to half maximum. After a 30-minute rest with one Ration, everyone recovers all HP; one Ration feeds the whole party. If combat interrupts the meal, no healing occurs before combat, but the party can resume the rest from where it stopped.
fields.title: Healing

fields.text: Henchmen cost 1s per day or half a share of loot, whichever is higher. They have 10 inventory slots, willingly carry torches, accompany the party through the dungeon, and neither take risks nor fight. Mercenaries cost 10s per day or a full loot share, whichever is higher, and stay near their employer. They accept risks including combat provided they are not asked to take more risk than everyone else. Mercenaries do not take separate combat turns: an adjacent mercenary grants the employer attack and damage bonuses. A level 1 fighter grants +2 Attack and +2 Damage and has a 50% chance to die instead when the employer would take lethal physical damage. Local-tavern mercenaries are level 1 fighters by default. A level 2 fighter grants +3 Attack and +3 Damage and can take two hits before dying. A level 1 thief grants +1 Attack and +1 Damage and can be persuaded to pick locks and scout rooms. A level 0 mercenary grants +1 Attack and +1 Damage. Every mercenary after the first contributes only +1 Attack.
fields.title: Hirelings

fields.text: At the start of each round, everyone makes a Wisdom check. Characters who succeed act before the monsters; characters who fail act after the monsters.
fields.title: Initiative

fields.text: Inventory slots equal Str plus the bonus from a container. A character without a container can carry only two things, one in each hand. A Burlap Sack gives +4 slots, a Backpack +7, and an Elfpack +10. One ration feeds the whole group. Bow ammunition is loosely tracked: mark one depletion after each encounter in which a bow is used; after three depletions, the character is out of ammunition.
fields.title: Inventory and Ammunition

fields.text: Investigation means a player specifically examines a feature or interacts with an object, such as opening a drawer, and usually takes negligible time. Searching means the party spends 10 minutes examining a room more closely, such as sifting through a bone pile. Anything discoverable through Investigation can also be found by Searching.
fields.title: Investigation and Searching

fields.text: Everyone begins with Common and no other language; nearly everyone, including goblins and morlocks, speaks some form of Common. Foreign languages are usually dead languages and are learned like Skills. A successful Language improvement grants 2 points instead of 1, but reaching 10 still requires a quest. Certain Languages grant an ability at 10 points.
fields.title: Languages

fields.text: A character levels whenever the party obtains a Treasure or reaches a Milestone, but not during combat. The lowest-level PC gains the level; break ties randomly. Every Treasure or Milestone also gives at least one person a Title chosen through discussion among the players and DM. At first level, HP becomes equal to Con, Atk becomes 1, and the player chooses a stat and rolls 1d6+1d4; if the roll exceeds that stat, it rises by 1. The character also chooses Fighter, Barbarian, Thief, or Acrobat. Additional classes are unlocked through play; see Appendix E.
fields.title: Leveling Up

fields.text: The dungeon is pitch black. Torches illuminate 30 feet and go out after two depletions; dropped torches can be recovered. Oil lamps illuminate 30 feet and go out after two depletions; dropping or throwing one creates a 10-foot-wide pool of fire for 3 rounds that deals 1d6 damage per round to anything remaining in contact with it. Candles illuminate 10 feet and last all day. Torches and lanterns deplete only on the regular Encounter Checks made every 30 minutes, not on checks caused by Noise. Light sources are extinguished if they fall in water.
fields.title: Light

fields.text: Each hireling begins with Loyalty 5. Asking for a dangerous task outside the hireling’s job description requires a Loyalty check and always reduces Loyalty by 1, whether accepted or not. Good treatment such as extra pay, extra safety, or respect raises Loyalty by 1 or 2. Mistreatment lowers it by 1, 1d4, or 1d6. At Loyalty 0, the hireling leaves at the earliest opportunity.
fields.title: Loyalty

fields.text: Map squares are 10 feet across. The DM describes the dungeon and the players map it themselves on graph paper; most rooms are 30 feet by 30 feet.
fields.title: Mapping

fields.text: 100 copper cuprek equals 10 silver shilavos equals 1 golden gorbel. When using gold as XP, 1 silver equals 1 XP.
fields.title: Money

fields.text: A monster that fears death flees rather than be destroyed; even elementals and undead recoil from annihilation. When morale calls for flight but escape is impossible, monsters attempt surrender. If the players appear not to take prisoners, they continue fighting. When uncertain whether a monster chooses intelligently, make an Int check for it. Chasing fleeing monsters uses the same Pursuit rules as player flight.
fields.title: Morale

fields.text: Difficult movement such as climbing, jumping, and fleeing uses a Move check, usually DC 16. A level 0 Peasant has Move 5. Falling deals 1d6 damage per 10 feet fallen. A character who intentionally jumps down can reduce the damage by 1d6 with a successful Dex check.
fields.title: Movement

fields.text: Whenever something makes Noise, roll a random encounter. The Lamb hears the Noise on 2-in-6 and arrives in 1d6 rounds.
fields.title: Noise

fields.text: First choose the direction of flight. The slowest party member makes a Movement check, usually DC 16; the Lamb instead has Slow DC 12. The party may drop items or alter the environment to slow pursuit. On failure, the fight moves into the next room and the pursuer takes a standard action, usually an attack. On success, the party enters the next room and the pursuer arrives at the end of the round. If the pursuer does not know the route, it chooses a random direction and continues for 1d4 rooms, preferring rooms it has not searched. Running past an enemy lets it make all its normal attacks. Hungry or Greedy enemies may stop for safely accessible food or money unless they have another reason to continue.
fields.title: Pursuit

fields.text: Each area has a local Encounter Table that determines who may appear. Every 30 minutes, roll the yellow Encounter Die and blue Recon Die simultaneously. The Encounter Die determines whether the result is Active, Passive, Indirect, or Depletion. An Active Encounter forces engagement, usually through a hostile creature. A Passive Encounter allows the party to choose whether to engage. An Indirect Encounter cannot be directly engaged but may provide information or establish the mood of the location.
fields.title: Random Encounter Checks

fields.text: The Recon Die is a blue d6 and succeeds on a 1. On an Active or Passive Encounter, success grants Surprise, allowing the party either to engage with surprise or avoid the encounter; the DM may also let the party overhear useful information. If no Active or Passive Encounter occurs, a successful Recon finds traces of a randomly rolled encounter, such as slime, hair, feces, graffiti, smells, or noises. With only candlelight, replace the Recon Die with an Ambush Die that surprises the party on a 1. With no light source, the party is ambushed on 1-2 on a d6.
fields.title: The Recon Die

fields.text: Saves use Dex, Con, or Cha against DC 20. Cha applies to all magical effects and is the most common Save. If a failed Save nearly kills a character, that character permanently gains +4 to that type of Save and records the event in the Legendarium on the back of the character sheet. Each character has 4 Save Slots.
fields.title: Saves

fields.text: An encounter entry begins with a general encounter, such as 1d6 goblins. If a Unique encounter is killed, it never appears again in that area. A second sentence may give a specific scene; use it the first time the encounter is rolled unless the DM prefers an original setup. On later rolls, create a new scene or build from the prior one. Place enemies where their arrival makes the most sense; randomly choose among equally plausible origins. Encounter placement must respect established topology and changes: enemies cannot emerge from an impossible dead end, and collapsing 12 ABACUS MURAL can make the south side safe from the Lamb if the Lamb remains trapped to the north.
fields.title: Setting the Stage

fields.text: Anything improvable through practice or study can be a Skill; all professions and college majors qualify. There is no fixed Skill list or fixed list of Skill uses. Social, perception, stealth, and direct combat Skills do not exist. At the end of each session, each PC may choose a Skill used or encountered during the session and make an Int check. Broad exposure counts, but the same book or library cannot teach the same subject twice. Success raises the Skill by 1, to a normal maximum of 9; the 10th point requires a quest. A character has 4 Skill Slots shared by Skills and Languages.
fields.title: Skills

fields.text: Lvl is the same as HD, and an enemy has 1d6 HP per HD. Def is the attack DC required to hit it. Atk gives the attack mode and damage, such as Claws 1d8. Move may be omitted when human-equivalent; escaping a slow pursuer is DC 12 and a fast pursuer is DC 20, and movement may instead name a comparable creature such as Climb spider. Unlisted stats default to 5 unless significantly different. A monster Int check can determine whether it behaves intelligently; failure makes it act like a dumb animal. Dis is disposition. If Dis is absent, the monster is average: it fights while it expects to win, then flees or surrenders.
fields.title: Stat Blocks

fields.text: Nearly all checks use DC 16. Roll 1d20, add the relevant stat, and meet or exceed the DC.
fields.title: Stat Checks

fields.text: A Stealth check is a difficult Dex check with a baseline DC of 20. The baseline scenario is approaching someone facing away without being heard and silently cutting their throat; adjust the DC for easier or harder circumstances. Failure means the character is spotted. Stealth is distinct from hiding: anyone can hide by describing how to the DM.
fields.title: Stealth

fields.text: A character wearing 0 or 1 piece of armor swims freely. With 2 pieces, swimming requires a Str check. With 3 pieces, the character sinks like a stone.
fields.title: Swimming

fields.text: Fists deal 1d3 damage. Improvised weapons attack at -2 and deal 1d6. Regular weapons deal 1d6. A two-handed weapon wielded by a character with Str 7 or more increases its damage die by one step. A magical weapon increases its damage die by one step. Damage dice increase from 1d6 to 1d8 to 1d10.
fields.title: Weapons and Armor

fields.appearance: A chicken vendor seated in the plaza beside the White Temple, visible through the fist-sized opening at the end of 15 CRACK.
behavior: Threatens to tell the temple guards unless given a reason not to.
After the extortion issue is handled, sells mundane items at the highest price he can obtain, never below 20 times market value.
Will run across town to purchase requested goods, taking 1-3 hours depending on the item.
goals: Extract as much payment or leverage as possible from the party.

reactions.response: He extorts them by threatening to inform the temple guards.
reactions.stimulus: The party first contacts him through the crack.

fields.role: An extortionate outside contact and merchant who can sell or fetch mundane goods.
fields.title: Danjo

behavior: Two hours after the Lamb is killed, he enters the dungeon with his bodyguards to check on it.
If the Lamb is dead, he hunts the Lamb’s murderers.
capabilities: Lvl 3; Def chain; Warfork 1d8; Dis wrathful.
Spells: delay, haste, scry.
As a Nemesis, each time he kills a PC he gains a level and is thereafter introduced as “Bastoval, Slayer of X”.

relationships.relationship: Bodyguard accompanying Bastoval.
Bodyguard accompanying Bastoval.

fields.role: The Lamb’s father and a Nemesis who enters the dungeon with two elderly bodyguards after the Lamb is killed.
fields.title: Father Bastoval

behavior: Friendly.
fields.role: A friendly rat encountered in 11 CRAB MURAL.
fields.title: Friendly Rat

behavior: If the Lamb is killed but its corpse is not utterly destroyed, they wait quietly and then chew out of the corpse.
They will not swim out to the cistern.
They have a 2-in-6 chance to ambush from the ceiling and grapple only during the surprise round.
capabilities: Lvl 2; Def chain; Bite 1d8; Move human; Climb as slug; Str 5; Int 3; Dis hungry.
Immune to acid.
Will not approach within 10 feet of burning oil because of bright light and fire.

reactions.response: They avoid approaching within 10 feet of burning oil.
reactions.stimulus: Bright light, fire, or burning oil is nearby.

fields.role: Three offspring that emerge from the Lamb’s corpse and hunt as ceiling-climbing predators.
fields.title: The Little Lambs

fields.appearance: A live goat tied with short twine and wearing a bell.
behavior: Friendly.
fields.role: A friendly, dehydrated animal in 2 GOATS.
starting_state: Dehydrated and tied with short twine.
fields.title: Live Goat

capabilities: Lvl 1; Def plate; Mace 1d6.
Carries a bow that deals 1d6 damage.

relationships.relationship: Bodyguard serving and accompanying Father Bastoval.
The other member of the elderly bodyguard pair.

fields.role: One of Father Bastoval’s elderly bodyguards.
fields.title: Mino

fields.appearance: A robed skeleton seated against the wall, holding out a black iron spellbook and balancing a crystal goblet on its knee.
behavior: Offers a black iron spellbook.
Clutches a delicate crystal goblet close to its body.
fields.role: A dead figure in 14A SHADRAKUL that presents the spellbook and anchors a serpent-and-goblet trap.
fields.title: Robed Skeleton

behavior: Lunges out and attacks anyone who approaches the skeleton.
capabilities: Lvl 1; Def chain; Bite: save or die; Dis guardian.
fields.role: A concealed guardian that lunges from the robed skeleton when anyone approaches.
fields.title: Skeletal Serpent

fields.appearance: A gigantic, hairless, obese cow-like creature with no obvious head; its neck ends in a drooping cowl of wrinkled flesh, from which it can extend a bloody horse-skull head with sunken eyes and a black tongue. It weighs about 2500 lbs, drags its belly, and reeks of blood and ammonia.
behavior: Mostly remains in 8 PIT and 9 FOUNTAIN.
Its sight and hearing are slightly worse than an average human’s.
It is not smart but is clever, learns from mistakes, and adopts better tactics with exposure.
If it finishes eating or loses track of the party, it heads to 9 FOUNTAIN for a bath.
capabilities: Lvl 6; Def chain; Bite/Crush 1d8/1d18; Move slow; Climb slug; Str 9; Int 3; Dis hungry.
Immune to acid.
Torches and lanterns make it hesitate, but only a large fire scares it away.
If people try to run past it in a hallway or room, it makes both attacks.
Can climb out of 8 PIT in 2 rounds.
Carries 52 Nascent Lambfruit and 6 Immature Lambfruit.

reactions.response: It calls “Father! Father!” in increasingly loud tones; it can say nothing else.
reactions.stimulus: It is wounded or scared.

reactions.response: It devours one restrained human at random over 10 minutes and is not very alert while eating.
reactions.stimulus: People hide from it during the opening encounter.

reactions.response: It attacks.
reactions.stimulus: People flee noisily during the opening encounter.

reactions.response: It does not notice them.
reactions.stimulus: People leave slowly and quietly during the opening encounter.

reactions.response: It becomes cunning and begins blocking the crawl tunnel with bones.
reactions.stimulus: It has experienced 3 encounters with the party near 10 BONE PILE.

fields.role: The dungeon’s central predator, guarding and roaming between its pit and fountain.
starting_state: Lumbering into 1 BOWLS as the game begins.
fields.title: The Lamb

fields.text: Removing the supporting pike collapses the ceiling. Grabbing the pike and running requires a Movement check to avoid dying, and the room becomes impassable.
fields.title: Collapsed Abacus-Mural Room

fields.text: Each time Father Bastoval kills a PC, he gains a level, and the GM thereafter introduces him as “Bastoval, Slayer of X”.
fields.title: Bastoval’s Nemesis Advancement

fields.text: Anyone with a lobster claw is Favored by Vandoh.
fields.title: Favored by Vandoh

fields.text: The first person to enter 9 FOUNTAIN falls, gasps, and flops for 1 round while hallucinating that heavy armor traps them underwater.
fields.title: Drowning Hallucination

fields.text: The first person to touch the fountain water is shoved in with no save. The water weighs that person down so no part of the body can exit, while a man’s death-gasps fill the air. The water behaves normally for everyone else.
fields.title: Haunted Water Binding

fields.text: When the Lamb is killed, the earth trembles as Vandoh mourns his child.
fields.title: Earth Tremor on the Lamb’s Death

fields.text: Killing the Lamb counts as a Milestone.
fields.title: Lamb-Kill Milestone

fields.text: If the ceiling collapses on the Lamb, it takes 3d6 damage, digs out in 30 minutes—probably on the north side—and is helpless for 1 round as it exits. Digging can be heard by anyone investigating the rubble.
fields.title: Lamb Trapped by Collapse

fields.text: If the Lamb is killed but its corpse is not utterly destroyed, three Little Lambs wait quietly and then chew their way out.
fields.title: Little Lamb Emergence

fields.text: If the armored skeleton is destroyed to end the haunting, the destroyer must make a Charisma Save; on a failure, the destroyer becomes permanently afraid of water.
fields.title: Permanent Fear of Water

fields.text: Each minute in 15 CRACK has a 50% chance of a bite. A first bite causes wheezing and muteness for 1 hour; a second bite causes instant death with no Save.
fields.title: Red Spider Bites

fields.text: The sarcophagus lid edges are sharp enough to cut ropes and sever ropes when the trapdoor dumps an occupant.
fields.title: Bladed Sarcophagus Rope-Cut

fields.text: The skeletal serpent’s bite requires a save or causes death.
fields.title: Skeletal Serpent Bite

fields.text: Sitting on the throne counts as a Milestone.
fields.title: Throne Milestone

fields.text: A successful Charisma Save turns the right hand into a large lobster claw dealing 1d8. A failed save adds 3 Inventory Slots of fat and turns the right hand into a small lobster claw dealing 1d6.
fields.title: Throne Transformation

fields.text: Regardless of the throne save result, the sitter sees a vision of a purple book wrapped in fine copper chains.
fields.title: Vision of the Chained Purple Book

fields.text: On an incorrect tumbler entry, milky acid sprays once and deals 1d6 diminishing damage each turn until rinsed off.
fields.title: Milky Acid Spray

fields.text: Carelessly opening the chest in 17 ALTAR exposes the opener to yellow mold poison for 1d6 damage.
fields.title: Yellow Mold Poison

fields.text: A roll of 14 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a battered shield.
fields.title: Battered Shield

fields.text: A roll of 16 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a 30-foot rope.
fields.title: 30-Foot Rope from the Bone Pile

fields.text: A roll of 15 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a spear.
fields.title: Spear

fields.text: A roll of 17 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a torch.
fields.title: Torch from the Bone Pile

fields.text: A 10-foot wooden pike supports the sagging roof in 12 ABACUS MURAL; removing it collapses the ceiling.
fields.title: 10-Foot Wooden Pike

fields.text: An unused torch hangs on the wall in 14 SARCOPHAGUS.
fields.title: Unused Torch at 14 SARCOPHAGUS

fields.text: Eight soft rugs cushion the 10-foot fall into 14A SHADRAKUL and are worth 400s.
fields.title: Eight Soft Rugs

fields.text: A hidden drawer in the altar at 17 ALTAR contains one white candle.
fields.title: White Candle

fields.text: Searching the fallen-elevator wreckage in 18 SHAFT reveals a block and tackle.
fields.title: Block and Tackle

fields.text: The armored corpse has a helmet that is too large to pass through the portcullis.
fields.title: Helmet Beyond the Portcullis

fields.text: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries a bow and arrows.
fields.title: Bow and Arrows

fields.text: An iron spike lies on 18A LEDGE.
fields.title: Iron Spike

fields.text: A 30-foot rope lies on 18A LEDGE.
fields.title: 30-Foot Rope at 18A LEDGE

fields.text: All four goats in 2 GOATS wear bells.
fields.title: Goat Bells

fields.text: A pile of hay lies in 2 GOATS.
fields.title: Pile of Hay

fields.text: Short lengths of twine tie the goats in 2 GOATS.
fields.title: Short Lengths of Twine

fields.text: An empty wooden bowl is in 2 GOATS.
fields.title: Empty Wooden Bowl

fields.text: An empty wine bottle is found by investigating the vinegar trough in 3 VINEGAR.
fields.title: Empty Wine Bottle

fields.text: One immature Lambfruit rests on the wooden table in 4 CHESTS; see Appendix D.
fields.title: Immature Lambfruit

fields.text: A masterwork helmet with a smiling face and squinting eyes is inside the wooden chest in 4 CHESTS.
fields.title: Masterwork Helmet

fields.text: One torch is inside the wooden chest in 4 CHESTS.
fields.title: Torch from 4 CHESTS

fields.text: A fire striker rests atop the locked chest at 5 LANDING.
fields.title: Fire Striker

fields.text: A fresh torch is inside the locked iron-banded chest at 5 LANDING.
fields.title: Fresh Torch

fields.text: The metal torch holder at 5 LANDING is a 6-foot iron pole that can be pried out with difficulty.
fields.title: 6-Foot Iron Torch-Holder Pole

fields.text: A vial of lamp oil is inside the locked chest at 5 LANDING; the listed destructive opening methods break it.
fields.title: Vial of Lamp Oil

fields.text: A lit torch atop a metal pole can be picked up easily and will burn for another hour.
fields.title: Lit Torch at 5 LANDING

fields.text: A broom is in 5A CLOSET.
fields.title: Broom

fields.text: A gong and hammer are in 5A CLOSET.
fields.title: Gong and Hammer

fields.text: The robed skeleton in 14A SHADRAKUL offers a black iron spellbook; once it is held, the sarcophagus trapdoor locks open. See Appendix A.
fields.title: Black Iron Spellbook

fields.text: 10 BONE PILE contains 255 pellets, each holding about 100 pounds of compressed bone fragments only slightly smoothed by digestion.
fields.title: Bone Pellets

fields.text: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries a sword bearing a conidiopore insignia.
fields.title: Sword with Conidiopore Insignia

fields.text: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries a signet ring worth 50s with a conidiospore insignia.
fields.title: Signet Ring with Conidiospore Insignia

fields.text: A delicate crystal goblet worth 800s is balanced on the skeleton’s knee; the slightest touch makes it tumble and break.
fields.title: Delicate Crystal Goblet

fields.text: Danjo currently sells bread, never for less than 20 times market value.
fields.title: Danjo’s Bread

fields.text: Danjo currently sells candles, never for less than 20 times market value.
fields.title: Danjo’s Candles

fields.text: Danjo currently sells chickens, never for less than 20 times market value.
fields.title: Danjo’s Chickens

fields.text: Danjo currently sells a knife, never for less than 20 times market value.
fields.title: Danjo’s Knife

fields.text: A roll of 20 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a bottle of fine wine worth 30s.
fields.title: Bottle of Fine Wine

fields.text: A golden sensory-deprivation helmet worth 700s is in 7 THRONE.
fields.title: Golden Sensory Deprivation Helmet

fields.text: A roll of 18 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a bottle of liquid hole; see Appendix A.
fields.title: Bottle of Liquid Hole

fields.text: A lotus pipe in 4 CHESTS fits into the masterwork helmet and is worth 100s.
fields.title: Lotus Pipe

fields.text: The armored corpse wears a masterwork breastplate that is too large to pass through the portcullis.
fields.title: Masterwork Breastplate

fields.text: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries an Orb of Indulgence worth 500s.
fields.title: Orb of Indulgence

fields.text: A purple pouch in 4 CHESTS contains 2 doses of purple lotus powder; see Appendix D.
fields.title: Purple Lotus Powder

fields.text: Akina carries the Ruby Ring of Wisdom, worth 1000s, and offers it in exchange for rescue.
fields.title: Ruby Ring of Wisdom

fields.text: A silver-plate dageurrotype worth 50s shows a dozen strangely dressed men buried to their waists, facing the stars with mouths open.
fields.title: Silver-Plate Dageurrotype

fields.text: A roll of 19 on the Bone Pile Search table yields a silver bracelet shaped like veins, worth 100s.
fields.title: Silver Bracelet Shaped Like Veins

fields.text: The lead-and-iron chest in 4 CHESTS contains only the Skull of Davok, which escapes when the chest is opened; see Appendix A.
fields.title: Skull of Davok

fields.text: Akina can tell the party the basics about the White Temple, Vandoh, and the Lamb; the source does not provide those explanations on this page.
fields.title: Akina’s Knowledge

fields.text: The expected but not required sequence is: flee or hide, then return to free captives; lure the Lamb away from 9 FOUNTAIN and drink; follow the main path to 13 CITY MURAL, where the bashed-in door reinforces that locked doors can be broken; and escape through 21 HEAVY DOOR. Equipment such as light, rope, and weapons gates progress. The dungeon has one valuable but imperfect loop through a secret tunnel that the Lamb can eventually block. Deaths are expected, and the Lamb stopping to eat helps prevent a total party kill.
fields.title: Expected Dungeon Flow

fields.text: The four-digit password for 6 TUMBLERS is 1-2-1-2. The same pattern is signaled by the regular drips at 9 FOUNTAIN.
fields.title: Tumbler Password

contents: Three enormous stone bowls.
Each bowl contains 4 human sacrifices, bound hand and foot.
fields.first_impression: Three enormous stone bowls occupy the pitch-black room; each bowl contains bound human captives.
occupants: 12 human sacrifices, bound hand and foot.
fields.title: 1 BOWLS
triggers: The game begins here with the Lamb lumbering into the room.

contents: 255 bone pellets, each about 100 pounds.

discoverable.condition: Spend any amount of time searching the pile.
discoverable.information: A small crawl tunnel leads to 14 SARCOPHAGUS.

fields.first_impression: A pile contains 255 bone pellets, each holding about 100 pounds of compressed bone fragments only slightly smoothed by digestion.
hidden: After 3 encounters with the Lamb, it becomes cunning and begins blocking the crawl tunnel with bones.
resources: One d20 search result per man-hour, using the Bone Pile Search table.
fields.title: 10 BONE PILE
triggers: After 3 encounters with the Lamb, the Lamb begins blocking the crawl tunnel.

contents: Crab-grooming mural.
Locked wooden door to the east.
fields.first_impression: A mural shows a crab being groomed in a woman’s lap. A friendly rat is present, and a wooden door to the east is locked.
fields.title: 11 CRAB MURAL

contents: Mural of an impossible abacus.
Image of Vandoh performing a calculation.
10-foot wooden pike supporting the sagging roof.
fields.first_impression: A mural shows an impossible abacus with Vandoh, a polygon-headed man, calculating inside it. The sagging roof is held up by a 10-foot wooden pike.
hazards: Removing the pike collapses the ceiling; a person grabbing it and running must pass a Movement check to avoid dying.
fields.title: 12 ABACUS MURAL
triggers: Removing the supporting pike causes the ceiling to collapse and makes the room impassable.

contents: Mural of a city under the waves.
Huge spiderweb-filled crack along the south wall.
Moldy, locked, badly damaged eastern door.

discoverable.condition: Examine or try to manipulate the badly damaged door.
discoverable.information: The damaged eastern door can be quietly wrenched off its hinges.

fields.first_impression: A mural depicts a city under the waves. A huge spiderweb-filled crack runs along the south wall with a faint breeze coming through it; a moldy, badly damaged locked door blocks the east passage.
hidden: The Lamb previously damaged the eastern door by ramming it in a fit of madness.
fields.title: 13 CITY MURAL

contents: Unused torch on the wall.
Obvious crawl tunnel north to 10 BONE PILE.
Sarcophagus with bladed lid edges.
Inscription: “Shadrakul, who will not meet her apprentice in this life.”

discoverable.condition: Clear dust from the empty sarcophagus.
discoverable.information: A seam runs along the middle of the sarcophagus bottom.

discoverable.condition: Clear dust and inspect or tap the sarcophagus bottom.
discoverable.information: The bottom is metal and sounds hollow.

fields.first_impression: An unused wall torch hangs beside an obvious northward crawl tunnel and an empty sarcophagus inscribed “Shadrakul, who will not meet her apprentice in this life.” The lid edges are bladed.
hazards: The bladed lid edges are sharp enough to cut ropes and sever ropes when the trap operates.
hidden: Replacing the lid over an occupant opens the sarcophagus bottom and dumps the occupant into 14A SHADRAKUL.
Removing the lid again closes the bottom.
fields.title: 14 SARCOPHAGUS
triggers: Lifting or replacing the lid produces mechanical sounds from below.
Replacing the lid while someone is inside activates the trapdoor.

contents: Eight soft rugs worth 400s.
Robed skeleton against the wall.
Black iron spellbook.
Delicate crystal goblet worth 800s.
fields.first_impression: A 10-foot drop lands on eight soft rugs; a robed skeleton sits against the wall holding a black iron spellbook and a precariously balanced crystal goblet.
hazards: The slightest touch causes the crystal goblet to tumble and break.
Approaching the skeleton triggers a skeletal serpent attack.
hidden: Once the black iron spellbook is held, the trapdoor locks in the open position.
A skeletal serpent is concealed with the skeleton.
fields.title: 14A SHADRAKUL

contents: Hundreds of tiny red spiders.
Fist-sized opening overlooking the plaza beside the White Temple.
fields.first_impression: A very tight crack swarms with hundreds of tiny red spiders. A voice arguing about chicken quality can be heard, and daylight is visible at the far end.
hazards: Each minute of exposure has a 50% chance of a spider bite.
A first bite causes wheezing and muteness for 1 hour; a second bite causes instant death with no Save.
occupants: Danjo, a chicken vendor, sits outside the far opening.
fields.title: 15 CRACK

contents: A corpse-shaped mass covered in thick mold.
fields.first_impression: A moldy shape in the center of the room resembles a curled corpse hidden beneath thick fungus.
hidden: The shape is only mold, not a corpse.
fields.title: 16 MOLD

contents: Rotten wooden chest.
Rotten, worthless books inside the chest.
Silver-plate dageurrotype worth 50s inside the chest.
Altar with a sheep skull and faded flowers.

discoverable.condition: Investigate the altar.
discoverable.information: A concealed drawer in the altar contains one white candle.

fields.first_impression: A yellow-rotted wooden chest stands near an altar holding a sheep skull amid faded flowers.
hazards: Carelessly opening the chest exposes the opener to yellow mold poison for 1d6 damage.
fields.title: 17 ALTAR
triggers: Carelessly opening the chest triggers yellow mold exposure.

contents: Fallen elevator wreckage, 7 feet high.
Broken beams and loose bricks.
Loops of soft, rotten rope.
High shaft terminating 60 feet above.
Visible ledge 40 feet above.

discoverable.condition: Search the wreckage.
discoverable.information: A block and tackle is hidden in the wreckage.

fields.first_impression: A 7-foot-high heap of broken beams and bricks, apparently a shattered gazebo but actually a fallen elevator, sits amid loops of soft rotten rope. A shaft rises 60 feet, with a visible ledge 40 feet up.
fields.title: 18 SHAFT

contents: 30-foot rope.
Iron spike.
Sealed portcullis.
Armored corpse 10 feet beyond the portcullis.
fields.first_impression: A 30-foot rope and an iron spike lie before a sealed portcullis. Ten feet beyond the bars is an armored corpse.
hazards: The masterwork breastplate and helmet are too large to pass through the portcullis.
resources: The corpse can be pulled to the portcullis and looted for a sword, bow and arrows, signet ring, Orb of Indulgence, masterwork breastplate, and helmet.
fields.title: 18A LEDGE

fields.first_impression: A barnyard smell comes from the east.
fields.title: 1A FIRST INTERSECTION

fields.first_impression: A barnyard smell comes from the north, faint light comes from the east, and a vinegar smell comes from the south.
fields.title: 1B SECOND INTERSECTION

fields.first_impression: A vinegar smell comes from the west.
fields.title: 1C THIRD INTERSECTION

contents: Three dead goats.
One live goat, dehydrated and friendly.
Short lengths of twine tying the goats.
Bells worn by all four goats.
Pile of hay.
Wooden bowl, empty.
fields.first_impression: Three dead goats and one live, dehydrated goat are tied with short twine; all wear bells. A hay pile and an empty wooden bowl are nearby.
fields.title: 2 GOATS

contents: Stone trough half-filled with vinegar.
Empty stone trough that stinks of stale milk.

discoverable.condition: Investigate the reeking liquid.
discoverable.information: An empty wine bottle is in the vinegar trough.

fields.first_impression: One stone trough is half-filled with reeking vinegar; another empty trough smells of stale milk.
fields.title: 3 VINEGAR

contents: Locked wooden entrance door.
Wooden table holding 1 immature Lambfruit.
Wooden chest.
Lead-and-iron chest bolted to the floor and bound with two linchpinned chains.

discoverable.condition: Open the wooden chest.
discoverable.information: The wooden chest contains a masterwork helmet, 1 torch, 2 doses of purple lotus powder, and a lotus pipe.

discoverable.condition: Remove both linchpins and open the lead-and-iron chest.
discoverable.information: The lead-and-iron chest contains only the Skull of Davok.

fields.first_impression: A locked wooden door protects a room containing a wooden table, a wooden chest, and a lead-and-iron chest chained to the floor.
hazards: Removing the first linchpin causes headaches.
Removing the second linchpin causes nosebleeds.
fields.title: 4 CHESTS
triggers: Opening the lead-and-iron chest allows the Skull of Davok to escape.

contents: Heavy steel doors locked from the other side.
Ascending stairs barely visible behind the doors.
Lit torch atop a metal pole.
Sturdy table.
Locked iron-banded chest.
Fire striker atop the chest.

discoverable.condition: Open the locked iron-banded chest.
discoverable.information: The chest contains a fresh torch and a vial of lamp oil.

fields.first_impression: Heavy steel doors are locked from the far side, with ascending stairs barely visible behind them. A lit torch stands to the left; a sturdy table and locked iron-banded chest stand to the right. A horrible stench comes from the east.
hazards: Methods forceful enough to open the chest break the vial of lamp oil.
resources: Lit torch with about 1 hour of burn time remaining.
fields.title: 5 LANDING

contents: Broom.
Gong.
Hammer.
fields.first_impression: A small closet contains a broom, a gong, and a hammer.
fields.title: 5A CLOSET

contents: Statue of a fish with hands.
Four rotating disks, each showing a number from 1 to 8.
Recessed doorway impossible to force open.
Wall lever.
Tiny pool of milky acid.

discoverable.condition: Investigate the ceiling.
discoverable.information: A quartet of small acid nozzles is set in the ceiling.

fields.first_impression: A fish-with-hands statue holds four numbered rotating disks. A recessed doorway on the far wall cannot be forced open; a wall lever and a tiny pool of milky liquid are nearby.
hazards: An incorrect entry produces a horrible grinding noise every time and sprays milky acid once.
hidden: The room is a password-entry system.
The password is 1-2-1-2.
fields.title: 6 TUMBLERS
triggers: Pulling the lever checks the four-digit tumbler setting.

contents: Throne of sheep bones and unfired clay.
Golden sensory-deprivation helmet worth 700s.
fields.first_impression: A throne of sheep bones and unfired clay stands beside a golden sensory-deprivation helmet.
hidden: The throne works only once per year.
Anyone with a lobster claw is Favored by Vandoh.
Sitting on the throne is a Milestone.
fields.title: 7 THRONE
triggers: Sitting on the throne requires a Charisma Save and causes a transformation and vision.

contents: Slimy pit 40 feet deep and 30 feet across.
Knee-deep mud at the bottom.
Smooth stone walls.
fields.first_impression: A slimy pit, 40 feet deep and 30 feet across, has smooth stone walls, knee-deep mud at the bottom, and a strong ammonia-and-feces smell.
hazards: The pit is impossible to climb.
hidden: This is where the Lamb sleeps.
Akina cleans the Lamb of parasites and eats its vomit.
occupants: The Lamb is present 0% of the time on the first visit and 2-in-6 on subsequent visits.
fields.title: 8 PIT

contents: Slimy pool, 30 feet deep.
Dripping fountain shaped like a fish with hands.
Water dripping in a 1-2-1-2 pattern.

discoverable.condition: Investigate the pool.
discoverable.information: An armored skeleton lies in the shallows.

fields.first_impression: A 30-foot-deep slimy pool surrounds a dripping fountain shaped like a fish with hands. Its water falls in the regular rhythm “drip . . . drip drip . . . drip . . . drip drip.”
hazards: The first entrant hallucinates drowning for 1 round.
The first person to touch the water is pulled in with no save and cannot bring any body part out of the water.
hidden: The location is haunted.
The first person to touch the water is supernaturally shoved in and held beneath the surface.
occupants: The Lamb is present 100% of the time on the first visit and 2-in-6 on subsequent visits.
fields.title: 9 FOUNTAIN

contents: Connects to 44 CISTERN.
A person can swim the tunnel in 5 minutes.
fields.first_impression: An underwater tunnel leads away from the fountain pool.
fields.title: 9A UNDERWATER TUNNEL

contents: Rough-hewn stone walls.
fields.first_impression: A pitch-black dungeon of rough-hewn stone.
hazards: The dungeon is pitch black.
fields.title: Dungeon Features

contents: A fist-sized opening overlooking the plaza from 15 CRACK.
fields.first_impression: A plaza beside the White Temple lies beyond the fist-sized opening at the end of 15 CRACK; a chicken vendor sits there and can be seen through the opening.
fields.title: Plaza Beside the White Temple

steps: Clear the blockage by hand for 10 minutes.
Reopen the crawl tunnel.
fields.title: Clearing the Blocked Bone-Pile Tunnel
fields.trigger: The Lamb has blocked the crawl tunnel between 10 BONE PILE and 14 SARCOPHAGUS with bones.

steps: Grab the pike and run.
Make a Movement check to avoid dying in the collapse.
Make the room impassable after the ceiling falls.
If the Lamb is under the collapse, deal 3d6 damage; it digs out in 30 minutes, probably on the north side, and is helpless for 1 round as it exits.
fields.title: Collapsing 12 ABACUS MURAL
fields.trigger: A character removes the 10-foot wooden pike supporting the sagging roof.

steps: Locate the armored skeleton in the shallows by investigating the pool.
Either remove it from the water and pray over it sincerely, or destroy it.
If it is removed and prayed over, even the shortest sincere prayer ends the haunting.
If it is destroyed, the haunting ends, then the destroyer makes a Charisma Save; on a failure, the destroyer becomes permanently afraid of water.
fields.title: Ending the Fountain Haunting
fields.trigger: The party attempts to end the haunting in 9 FOUNTAIN.

steps: Pull the corpse to the sealed portcullis.
Remove items that fit through the bars: sword, bow and arrows, signet ring, and Orb of Indulgence.
Leave the masterwork breastplate and helmet behind because they are too large to pass through the portcullis.
fields.title: Looting the Corpse Beyond the Portcullis
fields.trigger: The party reaches 18A LEDGE and tries to recover the armored corpse’s equipment.

steps: Set each disk to a number from 1 to 8.

steps: State that the room is pitch black.
Apply dehydration to everyone: -4 to all rolls until they drink water; without water they die in 24 hours.
Begin everyone naked and possessing nothing, except one person has a knife.
Without a sack or backpack, limit each person to carrying two items.
Give each player control of 1 free character; their other characters remain restrained.

fields.role: One of the five trapped second-floor ghouls; he wanders with Luntz while pretending to be a gentleman and is associated with theater and politics.
fields.title: Jasper

fields.appearance: A 15' long creature, glossy like black rubber; when coiled it resembles a huge taut black rubber hose, and its searchlight is visible before the worm.
behavior: A coiled lantern worm is quiescent until touched or until light is brought near.
It retreats after it has eaten all available light sources.
capabilities: Lvl 4; Def leather; Slam 1d6; Crawl slow; Int 2; Dis hungry.

Eat Light: a targeted light source explodes and is destroyed; the worm eats the light and becomes brighter. The holder takes 1d6 fire damage unless a Wis Save negates it and is automatically blinded; everyone else is blinded on a failed Wis Save. A Con check each turn ends the blindness.
Lantern: sheds light in a narrow 60' cone. Whoever it looks at gets -4 to hit, also applying to adjacent people.
Stonemeld: can become a liquid and flow through stone, appearing as a wet dark stain.
fields.role: A hungry roaming or quiescent dungeon predator that seeks and consumes light sources.
fields.title: Lantern Worm

behavior: Wanders the halls with Jasper, pretending they are gentlemen returning from fine dining and entertainment.
When hungry, openly talks about hunger and performs friendship unconvincingly.
capabilities: Lvl 2; Def leather; Claw 1d6+agony; Move as human; Int 5; Str 7; Dis hungry.
Skilled in cooking, butchery, and lewd jokes.
goals: Satisfy his hunger for human meat.
hidden: His friendly overture at 21 HEAVY DOORS is a poor deception intended to create an opportunity to eat the party.

reactions.response: He and Jasper feign friendship while intending to eat the party at the first opportunity.
reactions.stimulus: The party fumbles with 21 HEAVY DOORS.

reactions.response: He and Jasper pretend to accept, then circle back and attack shortly afterward.
reactions.stimulus: The party offers dead bodies elsewhere as food.

reactions.response: He and Jasper are wandering the halls and can appear on the Random Encounter table.
reactions.stimulus: The party leaves and later returns.

fields.role: One of the five trapped second-floor ghouls; he wanders with Jasper while pretending to be a gentleman and is associated with cooking, butchery, and lewd jokes.
fields.title: Luntz

fields.role: A name printed in one passive-encounter entry beside Gerdith, discussing cavalry, archers, and infantry.
fields.title: Malenna

behavior: Hums tunelessly while endlessly polishing the ballista.
Complains and cracks jokes when Gerdith orders her to investigate.
Runs on all fours and behaves intelligently and ravenously.
capabilities: Lvl 2; Def plate; Halberd 1d8; Move as human; Int 5; Str 7; Dis hungry.
Skilled as a siege engineer and horse lover.
goals: Satisfy her hunger.
Continue her duties as a siege engineer and ballista guard.

relationships.relationship: Fellow armored ghoul and ballista guard; follows Gerdith on investigations while complaining.

fields.role: An armored ghoul who keeps watch over the company ballista in 27 BALLISTA and continually maintains it.
fields.title: Molina

fields.appearance: A monstrous, completely feral ghoul; when briefly seen from 37 CHEWED BONES, only his yellow eyes are visible before he growls and retreats.
behavior: Waits beside the opening after hearing the secret door open.
Growls and retreats into 39 STONE EGG if exposed by torchlight from a chair in 37 CHEWED BONES.
goals: Grab and eat the first person who climbs into the secret opening.
hidden: The other ghouls conceal where they imprisoned him.
He is waiting immediately beside the secret opening after it opens.

reactions.response: Shawson surprises them, grabs them, and drags them into 39 STONE EGG to eat them.
reactions.stimulus: The first person climbs into the opened secret passage from 37 CHEWED BONES.

reactions.response: He growls and retreats into 39 STONE EGG.
reactions.stimulus: Torchlight from a chair in the middle of 37 CHEWED BONES catches his eyes.

fields.role: A ghoul who lost his mind, was imprisoned by the other ghouls in 39 STONE EGG, and waits to ambush anyone opening the high secret passage from 37 CHEWED BONES.
fields.title: Shawson

fields.appearance: A pair of eyestalks can be seen protruding from the water 40' below the floor; they retract when the creature notices observers noticing them.
behavior: Retracts its eyestalks when it notices that it has been observed.
Watches for an opportunity from the water.
capabilities: The water surface is 40' below floor level.
The spider crab can reach 38' out of the water.
fields.role: A hidden predator below the traverse pit that watches for an opportunity.
fields.title: Spider Crab at 31 TRAVERSE

fields.text: Jasper and Luntz's ghoul claw attacks deal 1d6+agony.
fields.title: Agony

fields.text: The last ballista bolt in 27 BALLISTA deals 3d6 damage.
fields.title: Ballista Bolt Damage

fields.text: Any touch greater than a feather triggers the ceiling in 24 CRUSH HALLWAY. It takes 10 seconds to fall 10', rests for 10 seconds, then resets.

fields.text: Upon entry to 37 CHEWED BONES, the person closest to the heads in 40 GHOST FENCE feels their teeth chattering. The effect extends into 38 SHROUD as far as the heads can see.

fields.text: Anyone who returns the red silk battle standard to the Garrison of the Green Angel is invited to join them as a knight.

fields.text: A candelabra worth 20s sits on the banquet table in 36 TABLE.

fields.text: A set of plate mail bearing conidiaspore insignia is stored in 34 CACHE.
fields.title: Conidiaspore Plate Mail

fields.text: A wheeled ballista in 27 BALLISTA weighs 500 lbs and is named Conroy.

fields.text: Gerdith carries a Treasure: a crysmere blade of far Charcorra, clear as a black mirror. It is made from rare clays baked in a kiln for decades and functions as a masterwork sword.
fields.title: Crysmere Blade of Far Charcorra

fields.text: The crypts hold 7 mummified left arms in 25A, 7 right arms in 25B, 2 heads in 25C, 7 left legs in 25D, 7 torsos in 25E, and 7 right legs in 25F. Five additional costumed heads are in 29 STAGE. These parts can be reassembled and returned for the Vandoh favor outcome.

fields.title: Harpoon

fields.text: One of the seven mummified right arms in 25B has a hook-hand prosthesis.
fields.title: Hook-Hand Prosthesis

fields.text: A drawer in a rotten credenza on the furniture pile below 35 TRICKY HALLWAY contains 50s and a hooked net.

fields.text: The ballista's one remaining bolt is named Little Gerdith and deals 3d6 damage.
fields.title: Little Gerdith, Ballista Bolt

fields.text: 34 CACHE contains 2 blowtubes of mevverwen; Appendix D is referenced.
fields.title: Blowtubes of Mevverwen

fields.text: Molina wears 6 chalcedony rings worth 50s each and 2 topaz pendants worth 100s each.
fields.title: Molina's Chalcedony Rings and Topaz Pendants

fields.title: Flasks of Oil

fields.title: Purple Lotus Powder

fields.title: Purple Moon-Patterned Robes

fields.title: Red Mushroom Rampant Shield

fields.text: A silver platter worth 50s sits on the banquet table in 36 TABLE.
fields.title: Silver Platter

fields.text: Six silver shilavos are arranged at the foot of the harpoon in 33 FUNGUS to represent the ghouls.
fields.title: Six Silver Shilavos

fields.text: A cluster of large jelly-like eggs lies with the torsos in 25E. If kept near body heat or food, it hatches into 1d6 slobberworms in 24 hours.

fields.text: Searching the rubbish in 37 CHEWED BONES yields a spear with a shrunken head tied to it by its hair.
fields.title: Spear with a Shrunken Head

fields.text: 29 STAGE uses two rug-covered tables, two chairs, and a mock horse made from broken wood and corpse bits. The horse wears a ruined purple robe and has a saddle worth 20s.
fields.title: Stage Furniture and Mock Horse

fields.title: Magnificent Steel Pipe
