fields.title: Noisy Breach at 44A

activation.condition: The party chooses to fight the Lamb in the cistern instead of attacking it while it rests in 8 PIT.

approaches: Use harpoons, hooked nets, ropes, and burning oil in combination.
Fish for the Lamb with the hook hand and acceptable bait.
Ensnare the Lamb in the noria so the waterwheel drags and crushes it.
completion: The Lamb is killed in the cistern.
outcomes: The first acceptable hook-hand fishing attempt works automatically.
An ensnared Lamb can be dragged by the noria and crushed against the slotted ceiling.
A Lamb ejected into the White Temple's drinking fountain can bring a swift, forceful response.

participants.role: Primary enemy in the arena.

fields.perceived: The cistern becomes a difficult moving battle across deep water, boats, swimmers, pillars, and the operating noria.

possible_effects.condition: The party gets the Lamb ensnared in the noria.
possible_effects.description: The noria can crush and kill the ensnared Lamb against the slotted ceiling.
The White Temple may respond swiftly and forcefully if its godling is ejected into its drinking fountain.

stakes: The party must kill or survive the Lamb while movement is constrained by deep water.
Using the noria to kill the Lamb can provoke the White Temple.
fields.title: FIGHTING THE LAMB

fields.text: Anyone can become an Acrobat. Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and increases Nah to 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf. Dodge gives +2 Defense per empty inventory slot, capped at 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower, and does not stack with armor. Nah can declare once per day, or twice per day at Template C, that something physically dodgeable does not affect the Acrobat. Tricky makes a natural 20 attack deal double damage and grant a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver. Cat Power treats falls as 20 feet shorter and causes cats to tend to like the Acrobat. Roast the Oaf lets the Acrobat force a larger enemy that misses with a melee attack to make another melee attack against a target in range, potentially itself. Two copies of Tricky from two Acrobat and two Fighter levels combine into Very Tricky.
fields.title: Acrobat

fields.text: Anyone can become a Barbarian without first unlocking the class through play.
fields.title: Barbarian

fields.text: Cleric is an additional class that must be unlocked through play before its templates may be selected.
fields.title: Cleric

fields.text: Anyone can become a Fighter without first unlocking the class through play.
fields.title: Fighter

fields.text: Knight is an additional class that must be unlocked through play before its templates may be selected.
fields.title: Knight

fields.text: Tactician is an additional class that must be unlocked through play before its templates may be selected.
fields.title: Tactician

fields.text: Anyone can become a Thief without first unlocking the class through play.
fields.title: Thief

fields.text: Warlock is an additional class that must be unlocked through play before its templates may be selected.
fields.title: Warlock

fields.text: Wizard is an additional class that must be unlocked through play before its templates may be selected.
fields.title: Wizard

fields.text: Up to three times per day, the abacus can answer a qualifying question with an integer from 2 through 9. A secret d100 roll determines the result: 11–100 answers honestly, 2–9 answers with the rolled number, and 1 or 10 produces no response. Questions are limited to obdurate physical things within 100 feet, may contain no more than 12 words, and cannot depend on names, mind-reading, or reliable distinction between humans.
fields.title: Abacus of Vandoh Answers

fields.text: The Acrobat treats falls as if they were 20 feet shorter. Cats tend to like the Acrobat.
fields.title: Cat Power

fields.text: Each empty inventory slot grants +2 Defense, up to a maximum of 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower. This benefit does not stack with armor.
fields.title: Dodge

fields.text: The Acrobat may declare that something does not affect them, provided it is something they could physically dodge. Template A provides 1 use per day; Template C raises this to 2 uses per day.
fields.title: Nah

fields.text: Whenever a larger enemy misses the Acrobat with a melee attack, the Acrobat may force that enemy to make another melee attack against a target within range. The forced target may be the enemy itself.
fields.title: Roast the Oaf

fields.text: On a natural 20 attack roll, the Acrobat deals double damage and attempts a free combat maneuver. On a natural 19 attack roll, the Acrobat deals normal damage and attempts a free combat maneuver.
fields.title: Tricky

fields.text: Possession and study of the book permit a character to begin learning Cheoxic, provide the spells speak with dead and fear, and unlock leveling as a Necromancer. Reaching Necromancer Level 1 causes the lich Shadrakul to ask the character to become her apprentice.
fields.title: Black Iron Spellbook Instruction

fields.text: For [sum] rounds, each round the affected creature must name three fully distinct potential actions with no shared objects or verbs, then performs one chosen randomly by 1d3. A successful save negates the effect.
fields.title: Confusion Random Action

fields.text: While free of the lead-lined chest, Davok attempts once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet; a Cha Save prevents death. A successful absorption regrows much of Davok’s head and restores a thick, viscous voice.
fields.title: Davok Flesh Absorption

fields.text: Davok demands to be carried out of the dungeon and casts geas until someone complies. The geased thrall remains a playable PC but is utterly dedicated to serving Davok, will not tolerate words or actions against him, and calls Davok’s name when pressed. Once carried, Davok appears to sleep while searching the ether for fragments of his body.
fields.title: Davok’s Geased Thrall

fields.text: Davok awakens if touched or if his name is called. If he takes 10 damage in a single round, he is stunned for 1 minute while reconstructing himself. Returning him to the lead-lined chest makes him inert again; the dungeon contains nothing capable of destroying him.
fields.title: Davok Stun and Inertness

fields.text: With 1 hour of work, Davok can summon a carpet of vermin that carries the skull at a crawl. If he wanders the dungeon this way, he replaces Atmospheric Encounters on the Random Encounter Table for rooms 1–20.
fields.title: Davok Vermin Transport

fields.text: Once Davok is free, his loyal thrall becomes a warlock in his service, by force if the thrall refuses. The rest of the party may also enter Davok’s service or depart; if they depart, the newly made warlock becomes an allied NPC in Lon Barago.
fields.title: Davok Warlock Transformation

fields.text: A targeted effect is postponed for [dice] rounds. The spell can be cast as a no-time reaction outside the caster’s turn. Any paradoxes are resolved by the GM, with the source encouraging painful consequences for the caster.
fields.title: Delayed Effect

fields.text: The spell either evaporates 1 gallon of liquid, with a ×10 multiplier for each MD after the first, or deals [sum] damage to an animal foe. A Cha Save halves animal damage; dryness reduces or eliminates damage, while wetness can increase it.
fields.title: Dessicate Liquid or Animal

fields.text: The target is teleported to a random dungeon room, city street, or adjacent hex. A successful Cha Save negates the effect; room numbers determine a random dungeon destination.
fields.title: Emergency Exit Teleportation

fields.text: For [dice] weeks, the target must pursue a caster-chosen quest with a decent chance of success, while the caster must help. Neither participant may directly harm the other. Completion compels the caster to provide a proper reward. A successful save negates the binding.
fields.title: Geas Mutual Quest Binding

fields.text: The holder chooses the image shown by the mirror. Any imagined image can be displayed, including a truthful reflection.
fields.title: Hand Mirror of Lies Display

fields.text: For 3 rounds, the target exists at double speed; a creature gains one extra attack per round. The target also ages 1d6 years, and human hair permanently turns white. A successful save negates the effect.
fields.title: Haste Double Speed and Aging

fields.text: The target takes [sum] damage and catches fire. A successful Cha Save halves the damage and prevents the target from catching fire.
fields.title: Ignite Damage and Fire

fields.text: The consumer sees 6 seconds into the future as with precognition and must make a Con Save against nausea and vomiting.
fields.title: Immature Lambfruit Effects

fields.text: A creature that consumes the liquid turns into a self-aware boat and can communicate only through creaking.
fields.title: Liquid Boat Consumption

fields.text: Dispensed liquid becomes a boat according to quantity: a drop makes a toy boat; one quarter of the vial makes a 4-person rowboat; one half makes an 8-person small sloop; and the entire vial makes a full-size ship for 16. Insufficient space produces a deformed nonsense boat.
fields.title: Liquid Boat Manifestation

fields.text: Tasting the oil creates a large piercing-like hole in the tongue. Consuming it creates a hole in the abdomen and causes all of the consumer’s guts to fall out.
fields.title: Liquid Hole Consumption

fields.text: Applied to a surface, the oil creates a hole up to 6 inches wide and 5 feet deep. The hole cannot be wider than half the object, and separate holes cannot intersect; therefore perforating portcullis bars does not itself break them.
fields.title: Liquid Hole Surface Perforation

fields.text: The consumer sees one major future event with relative clarity.
fields.title: Mature Lambfruit Effects

fields.text: A target within 1 foot who has the powder blown into their face forgets the last 6 seconds without a save. Powder remains visibly on the face, but the target does not initially notice it.
fields.title: Mevverwen Memory Loss

fields.text: The consumer suffers nausea, vomiting, and rampant paranoia about the future.
fields.title: Nascent Lambfruit Effects

fields.text: The bearer’s next significant sin is immediately forgiven, and the silver orb then corrodes.
fields.title: Orb of Indulgence Forgiveness

fields.text: For [sum] rounds, the target is transformed according to one chosen adjective per invested MD: small, big, dangerous, harmless, mobile, or slow. Repeating big or dangerous twice intensifies it to very big or very dangerous; slow chosen three times can make the creature immobile. Without selected changes, the form is human-sized, self-defending, and roughly human-mobile. Investing 4 MD makes the transformation permanent. A successful save negates it.
fields.title: Polymorph Transformation

fields.text: The caster previews [dice] rounds of a specific proposed course of action through a roughly 20-second, no-dice solo exchange with the GM. The preview explores a possible future rather than applying it.
fields.title: Precognition Possible Future

fields.text: After smoking purple lotus powder, the character cannot sleep without smoking more until they have gone without sleep for 3 nights.
fields.title: Purple Lotus Sleep Dependence

fields.text: Smoking causes sleep for 1d3 hours. On waking, the GM rapidly narrates four dreams in random order: one fun, one about something that happened, one scary, and one about something likely to happen. At least one of the four should be semi-useful.
fields.title: Purple Lotus Sleep and Dreams

fields.text: For 1 round, the caster astrally projects to a point selected by direction and distance. Each MD beyond the first either makes the astral form invisible or increases the spell’s range by a factor of 10.
fields.title: Scry Astral Projection

fields.text: The favored character immediately receives a vision of a huge green fungal sun as the only illumination, while the character’s body becomes spores and a thousand distinct emotions are felt at once. The character gains one and only one casting of control emotions, and their eyes permanently turn green. On the first morning after leaving the dungeon, only that character sees a green glow beckoning toward the Many-Layered Hall. There the character is recognized as favored and offered a priesthood and the ability to level as a cleric of Shendormu, without any obligation to accept.
fields.title: Shendormu’s Favor

fields.text: A failed save puts the target into deep sleep. Noise cannot wake the target, but a slap or kick can.
fields.title: Sleep Deep Sleep

fields.text: Fed organic material, slobberworms produce additional slobberworms; with enough food, their population can double each day.
fields.title: Slobberworm Reproduction

fields.text: A fed slobberworm produces a large amount of extremely slippery slime, functioning as grease, whenever it is squeezed.
fields.title: Slobberworm Slime

fields.text: For 30 minutes after smoking, the user cannot move on their own or take actions, can speak with amphibians and reptiles, and finds colors, patterns, and croaking noises indescribably delightful.
fields.title: Toad Shavings Intoxication

fields.text: The favored character is immediately transformed: a visible third eye with a white sclera and still whiter iris opens on the forehead, the world becomes translucent except for the apex of the White Temple, and the character feels drawn there. The character gains one and only one casting of clairvoyance. The third eye then vanishes, leaving a vertical forehead wrinkle. On the first morning after leaving the dungeon, an origami bird lands and becomes an inert letter from Vandoh’s priests. The letter explains that the character should have been recruited rather than offered to the Lamb and invites them to the White Temple for an optional priesthood and access to level as a cleric of Vandoh. The priests cannot locate the character and send many birds. Prompt arrival produces no hard feelings and impresses the priests; delay or failure to appear causes them to rescind the offer and become wrathful.
fields.title: Vandoh’s Favor

fields.text: All objects in a 20-foot cone take [sum] slashing damage; a successful Dex Save halves that damage.
fields.title: Wave of Mutilation Slashing Damage

fields.text: A maple, shale, and lapis-lazuli abacus that can perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and certain types of square roots. Three times per day it answers a question whose answer is an integer from 2 through 9. The GM secretly rolls d100: 11–100 gives the honest answer, 2–9 gives that rolled number, and 1 or 10 gives no response. It cannot answer about things more than 100 feet away; it only understands obdurate physical things, cannot read minds or understand names, struggles to distinguish humans, and cannot understand questions longer than 12 words.
fields.title: Abacus of Vandoh

fields.text: A spellbook whose covers and pages are polished iron sheets, with letters formed by unpolished sections. A chain woven through its spine is intended to secure it to the owner’s waist. It is written in Cheoxic, permits a character to begin learning Cheoxic, contains the spells speak with dead and fear, and permits advancement as a Necromancer. Once the reader reaches Necromancer Level 1, the lich Shadrakul asks that character to become her apprentice.
fields.title: Black Iron Spellbook

fields.text: A hand mirror shaped like the outline of a woman’s face, including ears and carefully styled hair. Its holder chooses what appears in the mirror; it can display anything the holder imagines, including an honest reflection.
fields.title: Hand Mirror of Lies

fields.text: Orange Lambfruit. The Lamb currently bears 6. Consuming it allows the user to see 6 seconds into the future, as with precognition, and requires a Con Save against nausea and vomiting.
fields.title: Immature Lambfruit

fields.text: A vial containing a full-size ship in liquid form; it smells like the ocean and tastes like tarred wood. One drop forms a toy boat, one quarter of the vial forms a rowboat for 4, one half forms a small sloop for 8, and the whole vial forms a full-size ship for 16. If space is insufficient, the result is a deformed nonsense boat. If consumed, the drinker becomes a self-aware boat that can communicate only by creaking.
fields.title: Liquid Boat

fields.text: A vial of utterly black oil that bends light toward itself, produces a lensing effect in the surrounding air, and has no smell. Tasting it creates a large piercing-like hole in the tongue. Applied to a surface, it creates a hole up to 6 inches wide and 5 feet deep, never wider than half the object; created holes cannot intersect. Applied to a portcullis, it can make the bars resemble Swiss cheese without breaking them. Consuming it creates a hole in the abdomen and causes the consumer’s guts to fall out.
fields.title: Liquid Hole

fields.text: Bright red Lambfruit. The Lamb currently bears 0. Consuming one allows the user to see one major future event with relative clarity.
fields.title: Mature Lambfruit

fields.text: A powder that can be blown into someone’s face from a range of 1 foot. The target forgets the previous 6 seconds with no save. Powder remains on the target’s face, though the target does not initially realize it.
fields.title: Mevverwen

fields.text: Dark green Lambfruit. The Lamb currently bears 52. Consuming it causes nausea, vomiting, and rampant paranoia about the future.
fields.title: Nascent Lambfruit

fields.text: A silver orb about 1 inch across. It immediately forgives the bearer’s next significant sin, after which the orb corrodes. Orbs are sold but tightly controlled; the source states that finding one makes resale to the Church the only ethical option. It is worth 500s. Rumors claim that golden orbs can forgive even mortal sins.
fields.title: Orb of Indulgence

fields.text: A smoked drug that causes 1d3 hours of sleep. On waking, the GM rapidly presents, in random order, a fun dream, a dream of something that happened, a scary dream, and a dream of something likely to happen; at least one should be semi-useful. A smoker thereafter cannot sleep without more purple lotus powder unless they have remained sleepless for 3 nights.
fields.title: Purple Lotus Powder

fields.text: The remnant of the demon Davok, resembling a deformed elephant skull. Once released from its lead-lined chest, it tries once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet (Cha Save or die). After absorbing flesh it regrows much of its head and voice, demands to be carried out, and casts geas until obeyed. It can spend an hour calling a carpet of vermin to carry it at a crawl; if it wanders this way, add Davok to the Random Encounter Table in place of Atmospheric Encounters for rooms 1–20. It awakens when touched or when its name is called. In combat it casts ignite for 3d6 fire damage (Dex for half) and polymorph with 3 MD. Taking 10 damage in one round stuns it for 1 minute while it reconstructs itself; nothing in this dungeon can destroy it. Returning it to the lead-lined chest makes it inert. Once free it searches for its missing body parts, and its loyal thrall becomes a warlock in Davok’s service, forcibly if necessary. The rest of the party may join Davok or leave; if they leave, the new warlock becomes an allied NPC in Lon Barago.
fields.title: Skull of Davok

fields.text: Harmless, disgusting creatures resembling fat maggots the size of mice. When fed organic material, they produce flatus, more slobberworms, and a large amount of extremely slippery slime equivalent to grease whenever squeezed. They can eat anything a brave pig could eat, and with enough food their population can double every day.
fields.title: Slobberworms

fields.text: A smoked drug. For 30 minutes, the user is so intoxicated that they cannot move independently or take actions, can speak with amphibians and reptiles, and experiences colors, patterns, and croaking noises as indescribably delightful.
fields.title: Toad Shavings

fields.text: For an Acrobat with Cat Power, reduce the effective length of every fall by 20 feet.
fields.title: Cat Power Falling Distance

fields.text: For an Acrobat with Dodge, each empty inventory slot adds +2 Defense. Defense from Dodge is capped at the lower of 16 and 10 + Dex, and cannot stack with armor.
fields.title: Dodge Defense Calculation

fields.text: A character with two Acrobat levels and two Fighter levels has two copies of Tricky; those copies combine into Very Tricky.
fields.title: Acrobat and Fighter Multiclass: Very Tricky

fields.text: Nah may be used only against something the Acrobat could physically dodge. It is usable 1/day at Template A and 2/day at Template C.
fields.title: Nah Uses

fields.text: Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and Nah 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf.
fields.title: Acrobat Progression

fields.text: When a larger enemy misses the Acrobat with a melee attack, the Acrobat may force it to make another melee attack against any target in range, including itself.
fields.title: Roast the Oaf Retaliation

fields.text: A natural 20 attack with Tricky deals double damage and grants a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver.
fields.title: Tricky Attack Results

fields.text: Whenever a character gains a template, they choose a class and gain the corresponding template. Lower templates in a class must be gained before higher ones. Multiclassing is unrestricted by selecting Template A from another class. A character may have no more than 4 templates, but beginning at Level 5 may swap templates out. Unless additional classes are unlocked through play, choices are limited to Acrobat, Barbarian, Fighter, and Thief. Wizard, Cleric, Warlock, Knight, Tactician, and races must be unlocked through play.
fields.title: Class Template Selection and Multiclassing

fields.text: When a character gains a level, HP, Attack, Templates, and Mastery advance according to the Level Advancement table. The first four gained levels each grant one template; beginning with Level 5, each additional level grants 1 Mastery.
fields.title: Level Advancement

fields.text: Rolling doubles or triples on MD causes harm to the caster. The page points to GLOG: Wizards for full rules and offers a simplified option: doubles deal 1d6 damage and triples deal 3d6 damage.
fields.title: Magic Dice Doubles and Triples

fields.text: A character gains the first Mastery Point at 5th level and one at every later level. A Mastery Point may alter an adjacent ally’s in-game d20 roll or damage roll after the dice land. It cannot affect magic dice, skill-up attempts, stat-up attempts, natural 1s or 20s, or the user’s own roll. It may turn a near miss into a success, reduce damage an ally takes, or increase damage an ally deals. Mastery Points replenish after a full night’s rest.
fields.title: Mastery Points

fields.text: A spellcasting monster has the spells listed in its statblock and a number of d6 Magic Dice (MD) equal to the number of spells it knows. Those dice begin in the monster’s mana pool.
fields.title: Monster Magic Dice Pool

fields.text: To cast, a monster chooses a spell, a target, and how many MD to invest, then rolls those MD. Dice showing 1, 2, or 3 return to the mana pool for later turns; dice showing 4, 5, or 6 are expended until the next day.
fields.title: Monster Spell Casting and Magic Dice Recovery

fields.text: Racial options, like the listed additional classes, must be unlocked through play.
fields.title: Races Must Be Unlocked Through Play

fields.text: Favor from Shendormu grants exactly one use of control emotions and permanently turns the recipient’s eyes green. On the first morning after the recipient leaves the dungeon, a private green glow leads to the Many-Layered Hall, where the recipient is offered an optional priesthood and access to level as a cleric of Shendormu.
fields.title: Shendormu’s Favor Progression

fields.text: In spell descriptions, [dice] is the number of rolled MD and [sum] is the total rolled on those MD.
fields.title: Spell [dice] and [sum] Notation

fields.text: A spell does not affect a target unless the rolled [sum] is at least equal to the target’s Level.
fields.title: Spell Level Threshold

fields.text: Spells are spirits, angels, or demons temporarily trapped in a symbolic pattern, such as a brain or book, and then fired like bullets from a gun.
fields.title: Spells as Bound Spirits

fields.text: A spell with the Splittable tag may be cast multiple times against multiple targets. All invested MD are rolled together, and doubles and triples are still evaluated normally.
fields.title: Splittable Spells

fields.text: Favor from Vandoh grants exactly one use of clairvoyance and leaves a vertical forehead wrinkle after a temporary visible third eye vanishes. On the first morning after leaving the dungeon, one of many origami-bird letters invites the recipient to the White Temple for an optional priesthood and access to level as a cleric of Vandoh. Prompt arrival preserves the offer and impresses the priests; delay or nonappearance makes them rescind it and become wrathful. The clerics have no way to identify the recipient’s location directly.
fields.title: Vandoh’s Favor Progression

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target 1 creature; duration [sum] rounds. Each round the target declares three potential actions that are fully distinct, sharing no objects or verbs. Roll 1d3; the target performs the corresponding action. A save negates the spell. Splittable.
fields.title: Confusion

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target 1 effect; duration [dice] rounds. Delays an effect—something happening to one object because of an interaction with another object or spell. It can delay incoming damage or prevent a sword from breaking until later. It may be cast as a reaction outside the caster’s turn and takes no time. The spell can create paradoxes, which the GM is encouraged to resolve in the way most painful to the caster.
fields.title: Delay

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target object; duration 0. Evaporates 1 gallon of liquid, multiplied by 10 for every MD beyond the first. Alternatively, it deals [sum] damage to an animal foe, with a Cha Save for half. Drier targets take less or no damage; wetter targets, such as oozes, take more.
fields.title: Dessicate

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target object; duration 0. Teleports the target to a random room in the dungeon, random street in the city, or random adjacent hex. A Cha Save negates the spell. Dungeon rooms are selected by room number.
fields.title: Emergency Exit

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target person; duration [dice] weeks. The target is bound to complete a quest chosen by the caster, and the caster is bound to help with that quest. Neither may directly harm the other. The quest must have a decent chance of success. When it is completed, the caster is compelled to reward the target properly. A save negates the spell.
fields.title: Geas

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target objects; duration 3 rounds. The target object or creature exists at double speed and ages 1d6 years. Human hair becomes permanently white. Creatures can make one extra attack each round. A save negates the spell. Splittable.
fields.title: Haste

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target object; duration 0. The target takes [sum] damage and catches fire. A Cha Save halves the damage and prevents ignition. Splittable.
fields.title: Ignite

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target creature; duration [sum] rounds. The target becomes a creature that may be small, big, dangerous, harmless, mobile, or slow. Choose one adjective for each MD invested. An adjective may be chosen twice to make the result very big or very dangerous; choosing slow three times can make it immobile. The default result is human-sized, able to defend itself, and about as mobile as a human, such as a goat. Investing 4 MD makes the transformation permanent. A save negates the spell. Splittable.
fields.title: Polymorph

fields.text: Range 0; target self; duration 0. The caster sees what will happen [dice] rounds into the future if following a specific course of action. Resolve this as a very quick solo game with the GM, using no dice and taking about 20 seconds, to explore that possible future.
fields.title: Precognition

fields.text: Range 10 feet; target point in space; duration 1 round. The caster astrally projects to a point designated by direction and distance. Each MD after the first may either make the astral form invisible or multiply the range by 10.
fields.title: Scry

fields.text: Range 30 feet; target creature; duration 0. The target must save or fall into a deep sleep. Noise does not wake the target, but a slap or kick does. Splittable.
fields.title: Sleep

fields.text: Range 20 feet; target 20-foot cone; duration 0. All objects in the cone take [sum] slashing damage. A Dex Save halves the damage.
fields.title: Wave of Mutilation

behavior: Return in exactly 12 hours to open the iron door in 5 LANDING.
goals: Keep the beast from escaping.
fields.role: In the traditional Level 1 setup, they lock the characters inside through the iron door in 5 LANDING to keep the beast from escaping, then return in exactly 12 hours to open the door.
fields.title: Townsfolk

fields.text: Each level of Barbarian grants +2 Loincloth HP. Advancement grants Rage at A, Firewater at B, Thews 1/day at C, and Rampage plus Thews 2/day at D.
fields.title: Barbarian

fields.text: Each level of Fighter grants +1 Attack. Advancement grants Stand Tough at A, Tricky at B, Very Tricky at C, and Double Attack at D.
fields.title: Fighter

fields.text: The dungeon contains 8 Treasures and Milestones used for advancement. As alternatives, level everyone when they escape the dungeon, or at the halfway point when they open 21 HEAVY DOOR.
fields.title: Level Ups

fields.text: Each level of Thief grants +1 Mastery and +1 Stealth. Advancement grants “Luck” at A, Opportunist at B, Preparation at C, and Snag at D.
fields.title: Thief

fields.text: After spending a turn drinking hard alcohol, the Barbarian heals 1d6+1 HP and gains 1 point of Drunkenness.
fields.title: Firewater

fields.text: While unarmored, the Barbarian's maximum HP increases by the character's Loincloth HP; each Barbarian level grants +2 Loincloth HP.
fields.title: Loincloth HP

fields.text: While raging, the Barbarian gains +1 Attack and +1 Damage and is immune to pain and fear. The Barbarian cannot do anything defensive, curative, or cooperative; mostly only attacks in different ways are possible, and any spell cast must be damaging.
fields.title: Rage

fields.text: The Barbarian's Rage bonuses improve to +2 Attack and +2 Damage.
fields.title: Rampage

fields.text: For one use, either treat Strength as 10 for one round, or make one attack with a +4 bonus that deals double damage on a hit. The attack bonus stacks with Rage.
fields.title: Thews

fields.text: Drunkenness expands the character's critical-fumble range by an amount equal to the character's Drunkenness points.
fields.title: Drunkenness

fields.text: The Fighter can attack twice per turn on the Fighter's turn.
fields.title: Double Attack

fields.text: Sacrificing a worn piece of armor reduces incoming damage by 1d6; sacrificing a held shield reduces incoming damage by 1d12.
fields.title: Stand Tough

fields.text: A natural 20 attack roll deals double damage and allows a free combat maneuver. A natural 19 deals regular damage and allows a free combat maneuver.
fields.title: Tricky

fields.text: Tricky expands to attack rolls of 18 and 19. Free combat maneuvers triggered by an 18, 19, or 20 gain +4 to the attempt.
fields.title: Very Tricky

fields.text: The Thief may spend Mastery points to benefit the Thief instead of being forced to help others.
fields.title: “Luck”

fields.text: When the Thief has a situational bonus on an attack roll, such as surprise or elevation, the attack deals an additional +1d6 damage.
fields.title: Opportunist

fields.text: In town, the Thief may obtain an Unmarked Package for 10s from an unspecified black market or shady alley. When opened or removed from the Thief's possession, it becomes a declared mundane item worth no more than 10s, representing prior foresight and effectively delivering the needed tool to the current location.
fields.title: Preparation

fields.text: After the Thief attacks an opponent, after an opponent attacks the Thief, or when the Thief walks past someone out of combat, the Thief may attempt to grab one eligible item from that target with a 2-in-6 chance of success.
fields.title: Snag

fields.text: A Treasure located in 39 STONE EGG and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.
fields.title: Abacus of Vandoh

fields.text: Room 17 contains 1 candle as a key light source.
fields.title: Candle

fields.text: A Treasure located in 27 BALLISTA and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.

fields.text: Room 20 contains Liquid Light as a key light source.
fields.title: Liquid Light

fields.text: Key light sources include 1 oil in room 5 and 2 oil each in rooms 24, 30, and 45.
fields.title: Oil

fields.title: Rope

fields.text: A Treasure located in 8 PIT and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.
fields.title: Ruby Ring of Wisdom

fields.text: Key light sources include 1 torch in room 4, 1.5 torches in room 5, 1 torch in room 10, and 1 torch in room 14.
fields.title: Torch

fields.text: 44 CISTERN is at the bottom of a well and can be used as an entrance when running the dungeon backwards.
fields.title: 44 CISTERN Well Access

fields.text: Opening 21 HEAVY DOOR is treated as the dungeon's halfway point for the suggested alternate level-up timing.
fields.title: 21 HEAVY DOOR as the Halfway Point

steps: Have the characters enter through 44 CISTERN, which is at the bottom of a well.
Remove the underwater tunnel and the wall from 44 CISTERN so section 2 is accessible.
Add an ooze to 14 MOLD.
Add a candle golem to 5 LANDING.
fields.title: Run the Dungeon Backwards from 44 CISTERN
fields.trigger: When preparing the dungeon to be played backwards.

steps: Use 21 HEAVY DOOR as the dungeon exit.
fields.title: Short Dungeon Exit at 21 HEAVY DOOR
fields.trigger: When preparing a shorter dungeon for a one-shot.

steps: Ignore rooms 1–20.
Use 21 HEAVY DOOR as the first room of the dungeon.
fields.title: Start at 21 HEAVY DOOR
fields.trigger: When omitting rooms 1–20.

steps: Have the characters enter through the iron door in 5 LANDING.
The townsfolk lock the door to keep the beast from escaping.
The townsfolk return to open the door in exactly 12 hours; the characters remain locked in until then.
fields.title: Traditional Level 1 Entrance
fields.trigger: When running a more traditional game with equipped Level 1 characters.

fields.text: Instead of the Treasure/Milestone system, level everyone when they escape the dungeon. Because escape may take multiple sessions, the GM may instead level everyone at the halfway point when they open 21 HEAVY DOOR.
fields.title: Alternate Level-Up Timing

fields.text: Using Firewater takes one turn of drinking hard alcohol, then restores 1d6+1 HP and adds 1 point of Drunkenness.
fields.title: Using Firewater

fields.text: A Barbarian may enter Rage at any time. Rage ends when all enemies are destroyed or driven off. At the end of each turn, the Barbarian may attempt to end Rage early with a 2-in-6 chance of success.
fields.title: Entering and Ending Rage

fields.text: At class rank C, Thews is usable once per day; at D, it is usable twice per day. Each use chooses either Strength 10 for one round or one +4 attack that deals double damage on a hit; the +4 stacks with Rage.
fields.title: Using Thews

fields.text: Double Attack permits two attacks per turn, made on the Fighter's own turn.
fields.title: Double Attack Turn

fields.text: After incoming damage, the Fighter may sacrifice either worn armor for 1d6 damage reduction or a held shield for 1d12 damage reduction. Stand Tough can be used once per combat.
fields.title: Using Stand Tough

fields.text: On a natural 20 attack roll, resolve double damage and a free combat maneuver; on a natural 19, resolve regular damage and a free combat maneuver.
fields.title: Tricky Attack-Roll Results

fields.text: Very Tricky causes natural 18 attack rolls to trigger Tricky as well. A free combat maneuver triggered by a natural 18, 19, or 20 receives +4 to its attempt.
fields.title: Very Tricky Combat Maneuvers

fields.text: “Luck” allows Mastery points to benefit the Thief personally instead of requiring that they help someone else.
fields.title: Spending Mastery with “Luck”

fields.text: Any situational bonus on the Thief's attack roll, including surprise or elevation, adds +1d6 damage.
fields.title: Opportunist Trigger

fields.text: Whether Snag succeeds or fails, the target is aware of the attempt. Out of combat, Snag may be attempted while walking past someone. After the first out-of-combat attempt against the same target, each additional attempt has a 50% chance of being noticed.
fields.title: Snag Awareness and Repeated Attempts

fields.text: Snag cannot take held or tightly worn items, such as a sword or armor. It can take other items, including rings and objects in pockets or backpacks. If no item is specified, steal an item at random.
fields.title: Snag Item Eligibility

fields.text: Preparation is used in town and costs 10s. The package's contents must be declared when the package is opened or leaves the Thief's possession, and the contents must be one mundane item worth no more than 10s.
fields.title: Unmarked Package Declaration

fields.text: The dungeon presents 8 advancement objectives: three Milestones and five Treasures. The listed objectives are sitting on the throne in 7 THRONE; finding the Ruby Ring of Wisdom in 8 PIT; finding the Jewelled Crab Bracer in 19 PRIESTS; removing the bar from 21 HEAVY DOOR or killing the Lamb; finding the Crysmere Blade of Charcorra in 27 BALLISTA; finding the Abacus of Vandoh in 39 STONE EGG; finding the Hand Mirror of Lies in 42 SUNKEN GALLERY; and escaping through 46B TOWER.
fields.title: Treasure and Milestone Level Ups

uncertainties.description: The map labels a vertical connection as 35A, while page 35 describes the trapdoor pit without a separate 35A heading. The node label and waypoint classification therefore combine the map label with that description.
The exact position and vertical profile of the entrance from 9 FOUNTAIN into 9A UNDERWATER TUNNEL are not stated in text; the map marks a concealed connection and the fountain pool is 30 feet deep.
The source states that 9A UNDERWATER TUNNEL connects to 44 CISTERN and takes about five minutes to swim, but does not state whether the tunnel rises, falls, or remains level.
The maps show a metal-door symbol between 41 SUNKEN SHRINE and 42 SUNKEN GALLERY, but the supplied room text does not identify its exact subtype or default state.
The maps show a metal-door symbol between 42 SUNKEN GALLERY and 43 SPIDER CRAB, but the supplied room text does not identify its exact subtype or default state.
The map shows a locked steel door east of 43 SPIDER CRAB, but the destination beyond that boundary is not identified on any supplied page.
Page 24 shows that 15 CRACK reaches a fist-sized opening overlooking the plaza and supports sight, speech, and exchange of small items, but it does not support person-sized traversal into the plaza.
Page 32 repeats the heading 25F CRYPT for two different moon phases, while the map distinctly labels rooms 25C and 25F. The node labels follow the map.
The ascending stairs behind the north steel doors at 5 LANDING are visible, but their destination is not named in this pack.

appearance.value: A gigantic, hairless, obese cow-like creature with no obvious head; its neck ends in a drooping cowl of wrinkled flesh, from which it can extend a bloody horse-skull head with sunken eyes and a black tongue. It weighs about 2500 lbs, drags its belly, and reeks of blood and ammonia.

value: Mostly remains in 8 PIT and 9 FOUNTAIN.
Its sight and hearing are slightly worse than an average human’s.
It is not smart but is clever, learns from mistakes, and adopts better tactics with exposure.
If it finishes eating or loses track of the party, it heads to 9 FOUNTAIN for a bath.
When someone enters the center of 44 CISTERN, it starts swimming toward them.
One round after beginning its approach, it urinates in anticipation and fills the air with an ammonia stink.
On the following round, it loses patience and begins swimming on the surface.
When noisy wall-breaking vibrations reach it, it arrives in 5+1d4 minutes and waits on the cistern bottom near the mouth of the underwater tunnel.
It rests in 8 PIT 2-in-6 of the time.
Lvl 6; Def chain; Bite/Crush 1d8/1d18; Move slow; Climb slug; Str 9; Int 3; Dis hungry.
Immune to acid.
Torches and lanterns make it hesitate, but only a large fire scares it away.
If people try to run past it in a hallway or room, it makes both attacks.
Can climb out of 8 PIT in 2 rounds.
Carries 52 Nascent Lambfruit and 6 Immature Lambfruit.
Produces the exotic types of waste stored in the four pools of area 20.
Swims 10 feet per round.
Climbs the slick walls at 46 DAYLIGHT as fast as a human can.
The author recommends attacking it in 8 PIT when it is resting there, using fire and sharp things while it struggles to climb out.
The White Temple regards it as their godling.

text.value: One of the classes available to choose when a character reaches first level.

Anyone can become an Acrobat. Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and increases Nah to 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf. Dodge gives +2 Defense per empty inventory slot, capped at 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower, and does not stack with armor. Nah can declare once per day, or twice per day at Template C, that something physically dodgeable does not affect the Acrobat. Tricky makes a natural 20 attack deal double damage and grant a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver. Cat Power treats falls as 20 feet shorter and causes cats to tend to like the Acrobat. Roast the Oaf lets the Acrobat force a larger enemy that misses with a melee attack to make another melee attack against a target in range, potentially itself. Two copies of Tricky from two Acrobat and two Fighter levels combine into Very Tricky.

text.value: The favored character is immediately transformed: a visible third eye with a white sclera and still whiter iris opens on the forehead, the world becomes translucent except for the apex of the White Temple, and the character feels drawn there. The character gains one and only one casting of clairvoyance. The third eye then vanishes, leaving a vertical forehead wrinkle. On the first morning after leaving the dungeon, an origami bird lands and becomes an inert letter from Vandoh’s priests. The letter explains that the character should have been recruited rather than offered to the Lamb and invites them to the White Temple for an optional priesthood and access to level as a cleric of Vandoh. The priests cannot locate the character and send many birds. Prompt arrival produces no hard feelings and impresses the priests; delay or failure to appear causes them to rescind the offer and become wrathful.

text.value: A Treasure called the Abacus of Vandoh is inside the opened Stone Egg; the source points to Appendix A for its full description.

A maple, shale, and lapis-lazuli abacus that can perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and certain types of square roots. Three times per day it answers a question whose answer is an integer from 2 through 9. The GM secretly rolls d100: 11–100 gives the honest answer, 2–9 gives that rolled number, and 1 or 10 gives no response. It cannot answer about things more than 100 feet away; it only understands obdurate physical things, cannot read minds or understand names, struggles to distinguish humans, and cannot understand questions longer than 12 words.
A Treasure located in 39 STONE EGG and counted among the dungeon's 8 Treasures and Milestones.

text.value: The lead-and-iron chest in 4 CHESTS contains only the Skull of Davok, which escapes when the chest is opened; see Appendix A.

The remnant of the demon Davok, resembling a deformed elephant skull. Once released from its lead-lined chest, it tries once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet (Cha Save or die). After absorbing flesh it regrows much of its head and voice, demands to be carried out, and casts geas until obeyed. It can spend an hour calling a carpet of vermin to carry it at a crawl; if it wanders this way, add Davok to the Random Encounter Table in place of Atmospheric Encounters for rooms 1–20. It awakens when touched or when its name is called. In combat it casts ignite for 3d6 fire damage (Dex for half) and polymorph with 3 MD. Taking 10 damage in one round stuns it for 1 minute while it reconstructs itself; nothing in this dungeon can destroy it. Returning it to the lead-lined chest makes it inert. Once free it searches for its missing body parts, and its loyal thrall becomes a warlock in Davok’s service, forcibly if necessary. The rest of the party may join Davok or leave; if they leave, the new warlock becomes an allied NPC in Lon Barago.

text.value: The ghouls first ask for human meat, lots of meat, destruction of the ghost fence in 40 GHOST FENCE, and humiliation of the spider crab in 31 TRAVERSE. If at least 3 are achieved, they also ask the party to beat Gerdith at a miniatures wargame in 28 GAMES, outperform Jasper at a show in 29 STAGE, and destroy the Lamb with cautious ghoul assistance. Each killed ghoul deducts one favor. At 4 favors they try very hard not to eat the party, requiring a Cha save to resist. At 5 favors the party's favorite ghoul joins. At 6 favors they reveal the door behind Captain Conroy in 33 FUNGUS and discuss their trauma. At 7 favors Gerdith gives her crysmere blade and they reveal Shawson's prison and magic item, though they will not help kill him.

text.value: At dungeon speed, characters are assumed to listen at doors before opening them; the DM reports audible activity behind a door. A wooden door can be kicked in with a successful Str check in negligible time, but doing so makes Noise; failure takes 10 minutes. Metal doors cannot be kicked in. Locked doors require the appropriate key or lockpicks plus a successful Locksmith roll. Portcullises have fist-sized gaps and are normally locked down so Strength cannot raise them; a nearby ratchet winch often raises them in 1 minute, and they drop in 1 second. A portcullis may instead be locked open. A barred door opens only from the barred side; each bar is a piece of lumber weighing more than 100 pounds, and moving one alone requires a Str check.

text.value: A level 0 character dies upon taking any damage. Other characters convert damage beyond HP into Lethal Damage, fall unconscious, and start Dying. At the end of each round, a Dying character makes a Con check at DC 15 + current Lethal Damage. Reaching 10 Lethal Damage causes death. An ally can spend an action to Stabilize the character with an Int check against the same DC. Any amount of magical healing also Stabilizes. Stabilization wakes the character and allows normal actions, but HP remains 0 and Lethal Damage is unchanged. Resting in town while safe and fed removes 1 Lethal Damage.

text.value: Henchmen cost 1s per day or half a share of loot, whichever is higher. They have 10 inventory slots, willingly carry torches, accompany the party through the dungeon, and neither take risks nor fight. Mercenaries cost 10s per day or a full loot share, whichever is higher, and stay near their employer. They accept risks including combat provided they are not asked to take more risk than everyone else. Mercenaries do not take separate combat turns: an adjacent mercenary grants the employer attack and damage bonuses. A level 1 fighter grants +2 Attack and +2 Damage and has a 50% chance to die instead when the employer would take lethal physical damage. Local-tavern mercenaries are level 1 fighters by default. A level 2 fighter grants +3 Attack and +3 Damage and can take two hits before dying. A level 1 thief grants +1 Attack and +1 Damage and can be persuaded to pick locks and scout rooms. A level 0 mercenary grants +1 Attack and +1 Damage. Every mercenary after the first contributes only +1 Attack.

text.value: The dungeon is pitch black. Torches illuminate 30 feet and go out after two depletions; dropped torches can be recovered. Oil lamps illuminate 30 feet and go out after two depletions; dropping or throwing one creates a 10-foot-wide pool of fire for 3 rounds that deals 1d6 damage per round to anything remaining in contact with it. Hungry or Greedy enemies may stop for safely accessible food or money unless they have another reason to continue.

text.value: The Recon Die is a blue d6 and succeeds on a 1. On an Active or Passive Encounter, success grants Surprise, allowing the party either to engage with surprise or avoid the encounter; the DM may also let the party overhear useful information. If no Active or Passive Encounter occurs, a successful Recon finds traces of a randomly rolled encounter, such as slime, hair, feces, graffiti, smells, or noises. With only candlelight, replace the Recon Die with an Ambush Die that surprises the party on a 1. With no light source, the party is ambushed on 1-2 on a d6.

values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Acrobat as an available class; pages 49–50 provide the class-selection rule, progression, and complete Acrobat abilities. The detailed class text is the canonical card content.
values.value: Anyone can become an Acrobat. Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and increases Nah to 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf. Dodge gives +2 Defense per empty inventory slot, capped at 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower, and does not stack with armor. Nah can declare once per day, or twice per day at Template C, that something physically dodgeable does not affect the Acrobat. Tricky makes a natural 20 attack deal double damage and grant a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver. Cat Power treats falls as 20 feet shorter and causes cats to tend to like the Acrobat. Roast the Oaf lets the Acrobat force a larger enemy that misses with a melee attack to make another melee attack against a target in range, potentially itself. Two copies of Tricky from two Acrobat and two Fighter levels combine into Very Tricky.

values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Barbarian as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 51 gives its progression. The detailed progression supersedes the generic class-list sentence.
values.value: Anyone can become a Barbarian without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Barbarian grants +2 Loincloth HP. Advancement grants Rage at A, Firewater at B, Thews 1/day at C, and Rampage plus Thews 2/day at D.

values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Fighter as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 52 gives its progression. The detailed progression is the canonical class text.
values.value: Anyone can become a Fighter without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Fighter grants +1 Attack. Advancement grants Stand Tough at A, Tricky at B, Very Tricky at C, and Double Attack at D.

values.rationale: Pages 2 and 5 describe complementary parts of the level-0 setup: their fragility and extra-life role, then the starting count and PC/hireling arrangement.
values.value: In this introductory adventure, every player controls multiple level 0 peasants. They have no special abilities and die in a single hit; the multiple peasants give players extra lives while they learn the system. The game begins with 12 level 0 peasants in a dungeon; unless there are more than 6 players, each player controls multiple peasants, choosing one as their PC and treating the rest as hirelings.

values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Thief as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 53 gives its progression. The detailed progression is canonical.
values.value: Anyone can become a Thief without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Thief grants +1 Mastery and +1 Stealth. Advancement grants Luck at A, Opportunist at B, Preparation at C, and Snag at D.

values.value: Removing the heavy bar from 21 HEAVY DOORS grants a Milestone because the party has escaped from the Lamb, unless the Lamb has already been killed. Reaching freedom outside the dungeon also counts as a Milestone.

values.rationale: The selected title covers both the heavy-door halfway escape and reaching freedom, which the cited pages present as milestone outcomes.

values.rationale: Pages 22, 32, and 37 describe distinct source triggers that grant the same named favor; the canonical effect records all three without inventing Appendix D mechanics.
values.value: A character with a lobster claw is Favored by Vandoh. If all seven mummies are reassembled and returned, or close enough, the character who took the most initiative becomes Favored by Vandoh. If all ghouls are killed, the character whose left hand was possessed becomes Favored by Vandoh; Appendix D gives the full effect.

values.rationale: Page 36 places the Treasure in the Stone Egg, page 43 supplies its mechanics, and page 54 confirms its Treasure status and location. The composed text preserves both placement and rules.
values.value: The Abacus of Vandoh is a Treasure in 39 STONE EGG. Made from maple, shale, and lapis lazuli, it performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, and certain square roots. Three times per day it answers a question whose answer is an integer from 2 through 9; secretly roll d100, with 11–100 giving the honest answer, 2–9 giving the rolled number, and 1 or 10 giving no response. It cannot answer about things more than 100 feet away, only understands obdurate physical things, cannot read minds or understand names, struggles to distinguish humans, and cannot understand questions longer than 12 words.

values.rationale: Page 24 establishes the encounter and location; page 43 supplies the spellbook's complete description and effects.
values.value: The robed skeleton in 14A SHADRAKUL offers a black iron spellbook. Its covers and pages are polished iron sheets with letters formed by unpolished sections; a chain is woven through the spine to secure it to the owner's waist. Written in Cheoxic, it lets a character begin learning Cheoxic, contains speak with dead and fear, and permits advancement as a Necromancer. Once the reader reaches Necromancer Level 1, Shadrakul asks that character to become her apprentice.

values.rationale: Page 23 identifies the bottle as a Bone Pile Search result and page 43 gives the complete Liquid Hole mechanics; the appendix description is the canonical item text.
values.value: A vial of utterly black oil that bends light toward itself, produces a lensing effect in the surrounding air, and has no smell. Tasting it creates a large piercing-like hole in the tongue. Applied to a surface, it creates a hole up to 6 inches wide and 5 feet deep, never wider than half the object; created holes cannot intersect. Applied to a portcullis, it can make the bars resemble Swiss cheese without breaking them. Consuming it creates a hole in the abdomen and causes the consumer's guts to fall out.

values.rationale: The appendix labels the item Liquid Hole; page 23's Bottle of Liquid Hole is the same item found in the dungeon.
values.value: Liquid Hole

values.rationale: Page 38 establishes the location and Treasure status, page 43 gives the full item description, and page 54 lists it among the dungeon's Treasures.
values.value: The crone's coffer in 42 SUNKEN GALLERY contains the Treasure called the Hand Mirror of Lies. It is shaped like the outline of a woman's face, complete with ears and carefully styled hair. The holder chooses what appears in the mirror; it can display anything the holder imagines, including an honest reflection.

values.rationale: Page 34 provides the concrete item placement and page 41 establishes its tactical use; these are complementary facts about one item type.

values.rationale: Pages 41 and 54 describe oil's tactical use and its keyed dungeon quantities; the values are complementary rather than competing descriptions.
values.value: Burning oil is a suggested weapon against the Lamb in the cistern, and the rowboat at 45 BARRELS contains 2 flasks of oil. Key light sources include 1 oil in room 5 and 2 oil each in rooms 24, 30, and 45.

values.rationale: Page 25 establishes the found item and value; page 43 supplies its mechanics, control, and rumor. The rumor is retained explicitly as rumor.
values.value: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries an Orb of Indulgence worth 500s. It is a silver orb about 1 inch across that immediately forgives the bearer's next significant sin, after which it corrodes. Orbs are sold but tightly controlled; the source says finding one makes resale to the Church the only ethical option. Rumors claim golden orbs can forgive even mortal sins.

values.rationale: Pages 21 and 34 record two separate dungeon caches, while page 48 gives the drug's complete mechanics; all facts concern the same item.
values.value: A purple pouch in 4 CHESTS and a small bag in 34 CACHE each contain 2 doses of purple lotus powder. When smoked, it causes 1d3 hours of sleep; on waking, the GM rapidly presents a fun dream, a dream of something that happened, a scary dream, and a dream of something likely to happen in random order, with at least one semi-useful. A smoker thereafter cannot sleep without more purple lotus powder unless they have remained sleepless for 3 nights.

values.rationale: Page 41 describes the tactical use and page 54 lists the keyed rope supplies; the canonical text preserves both.
values.value: Ropes are suggested tools that can be combined with other tactics to kill the Lamb in the cistern. Key items include 30-foot ropes in rooms 18A, 31, and 40.

values.rationale: Page 23 establishes Akina's possession and bargain; page 54 confirms the ring's Treasure and 8 PIT placement.
values.value: Akina carries the Ruby Ring of Wisdom, worth 1000s, and offers it in exchange for rescue. It is the Treasure in 8 PIT.

values.rationale: Page 21 establishes the chest and release trigger; page 44 provides the Skull of Davok's complete behavior and mechanics.
values.value: The lead-and-iron chest in 4 CHESTS contains only the Skull of Davok, which escapes when the chest is opened. The remnant of the demon Davok resembles a deformed elephant skull. Once freed, it tries once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet (Cha Save or die), regrows much of its head and voice after absorbing flesh, demands to be carried out, and casts geas until obeyed. It can call a carpet of vermin to carry it at a crawl; if it wanders this way, add Davok to the Random Encounter Table in place of Atmospheric Encounters for rooms 1–20. It awakens when touched or when its name is called, casts ignite and polymorph with 3 MD, is stunned for 1 minute by 10 damage in one round while reconstructing, cannot be destroyed in this dungeon, and becomes inert if returned to its lead-lined chest. Once free it searches for its missing body parts and forces its loyal thrall into Davok's service.

values.rationale: Page 34 establishes the dungeon cache and quantity; page 48 supplies the drug's complete effects and duration.
values.value: A small bag in 34 CACHE contains 3 doses of toad shavings. When smoked, the user cannot move independently or take actions for 30 minutes, can speak with amphibians and reptiles, and experiences colors, patterns, and croaking noises as indescribably delightful.
